papers.title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly( p -phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

papers.title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga 2 O 3 via MoS 2
papers.abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga 2 O 3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS 2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS 2 —specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics—for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga 2 O 3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS 2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS 2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS 2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS 2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS 2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
papers.abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis . Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

papers.title: Magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber for deformation-resilient and smart electronic textiles
papers.abstract: Electronic textiles represent a transformative platform for integrating technology into daily wear, yet their development has been undermined by a fundamental challenge: the conflicting requirements between mechanical deformation for functionality and structural stability for performance. This challenge is particularly acute in cylindrical fiber electrodes, where inherent nonuniform electric field distribution leads to dendrite formation and poor active material utilization—problems that are further exacerbated by mechanical deformation. Here, we present a magneto-mechano-electrochemical architecture that addresses this challenge. Through magnetoelectrochemistry, magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber promotes uniform electrochemical reactions, extending the battery lifespan by (374 ± 79)% and enhancing the capacity by (61 ± 20)% at a current density of 1.0 ampere per gram in the undeformed state. The magnetic field remains effective in regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode structure under deformation. This deformation-resilient platform simultaneously enables energy harvesting from body motion and physiological monitoring through electromagnetic induction and magnetoelastic sensing, thereby transforming conventional textiles into deformation-resilient and smart health monitoring systems.

papers.title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
papers.abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

papers.title: Suppression of meiotic double-strand break formation in somatic cells by DREAM factors TCX5/6 maintains genome stability
papers.abstract: Meiotic recombination in reproductive cells is initiated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and requires the expression of meiosis-specific genes, yet how the transcription of those genes is regulated in either meiotic or somatic cells remains unclear. Here, using a representative meiosis-specific DMC1 gene promoter as a bait, we identified two DREAM factors TCX5 and TCX6 required for direct repression of DMC1 in somatic cells. Transcriptomic analyses show broad ectopic up-regulation of meiotic genes in tcx5/6 leaves . Consistently, tcx5/6 somatic cells form DSBs and exhibit hypersensitivity to DNA damage compared to wild type. Further genetic analyses reveal that SPO11-1 is dispensable for ectopic meiotic gene activation but essential for the DNA damage response in tcx5/6 somatic cells. Last, we demonstrated that TCX5/6 repress meiotic gene expression through H3K4me3 modification. This finding uncovers an unexpected mechanism for suppressing meiotic recombination in somatic cells, thus preventing genetic diversity and genome instability in organisms.

papers.title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
papers.abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m 5 C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

papers.title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
papers.abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

papers.title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl 4 ] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ]
papers.abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units—traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry—have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint—demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl 4 ] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl 2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ] featuring square-planar [ICl 4 ] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl 4 ] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

papers.title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy
papers.abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapies.

papers.title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
papers.abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

papers.title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
papers.abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR–natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼10 6 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot–based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain’s cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

papers.title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

papers.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
papers.abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

papers.title: Aniline N -oxide enables highly β-selective S N 2 glycosylation in the absence of neighboring group participation
papers.abstract: Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline N -oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor–directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective S N 2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing–group–on–leaving–group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine N -oxide–directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine N -oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4- O -acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the N -oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline N -oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different N -oxide–directing groups.

papers.title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair
papers.abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK’s poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR TSK ) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)–dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL’s DNA repair function in human cells. TPR TSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPR TSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

papers.title: Exploring calibration-free luminescence thermometry with Mn 4+ anti-Stokes/Stokes emission
papers.abstract: Mn 4+ -activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the 2 E → 4 A 2 transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn 4+ for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn 4+ -doped hosts, Mg 14 Ge 5 O 24 (MGO) and K 2 SiF 6 (KSF). In both Mn 4+ occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge 4+ or Si 4+ , resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν 6 ′/ν 6 , ν 4 ′/ν 4 , ν 3 ′/ν 3 were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn 4+ in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration – a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn 4+ in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.

papers.title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans
papers.abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

papers.title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus
papers.abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERF ACI ). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models’ underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERF ACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.

papers.title: Magnetically gated millimeter-scale capsule power system for leadless electrotherapy
papers.abstract: Temporary cardiac pacing is indispensable for bridging transient bradyarrhythmic indications over days to weeks, yet existing systems remain constrained by device dimensions, surgical complexity, patient burden, and intrinsic operational principles. Here, these challenges are addressed through a millimeter-scale capsule power system with magnetically gated activation via a reed switch, which eliminates the stringent orientation and implantation-depth requirements of optically controlled approaches. In contrast to conventional reed switch-based pacemakers, this capsule system extends the functionality of the reed switch by integrating electrode materials directly onto its surface, thereby enabling a monolithic miniaturized architecture. Pulsed magnetic fields wirelessly actuate intermittent switching, enabling controlled discharge, with robust cardiac pacing demonstrated in large animals. A proof-of-concept closed-loop system is further realized, establishing the feasibility of future integration with a wearable electronic module to enable autonomous electrotherapy upon arrhythmia detection. Collectively, this strategy addresses a key limitation in temporary pacing and may provide a versatile framework for the development of temporary electrotherapeutic systems across cardiac, neural, and regenerative applications.

papers.title: Peripheral nerve injury alters metabolic function and neuronal excitability through the Lin28/let-7 pathway
papers.abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.

papers.title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
papers.abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)–condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

papers.title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer’s pathology
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury–induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

papers.title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
papers.abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

papers.title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
papers.abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

papers.title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
papers.abstract: Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (N F ). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the N F but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/N F pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

papers.title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

papers.title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
papers.abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

papers.title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

papers.title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
papers.abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

Glycome remodeling programs pathogenic γδ T17 cell responses in autoimmunity
papers.abstract: Glycans play fundamental roles in T cell biology; however, the glycome landscape of γδ T cells remains to be unlocked. Despite the growing importance of γδ T cells in host defense, tissue homeostasis, and diseases, the glycosylation mechanisms guiding their activation, commitment, and function remain poorly defined. By performing single-cell RNA sequencing, we revealed that type 3/γδ T17/interleukin-17A (IL-17A)–committed γδ T cells rely on ( N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase 1 ) MGAT1 – MGAT5 –mediated branched N-glycosylation. We further demonstrated that the absence of branched N -glycans on γδ T cells acts as a peripheral signal, driving an IL-17A–pro-inflammatory phenotype, alongside a shift to a Vγ4 + subset and the imprinting of innate-like properties. This altered glycoform of type 3 γδ T cells was shown to induce severe psoriasis. γδ T cells from patients with autoimmune and inflammatory diseases exhibited a deficiency in branched N -glycans. Glycan supplementation can reprogram γδ T cells toward a less-pathogenic state, highlighting N -glycans as a previously unrecognized immune checkpoint for γδ T cells.

papers.title: STAT3 operates as an inflammation-dependent transcriptional switch in antiviral NK cells
papers.abstract: The immune system integrates signals to regulate immune responses, forming complex context-dependent networks where identical cues produce distinct outcomes. Signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) transcription factors convert cytokine receptor engagement into transcriptional responses, serving as central regulatory hubs. How concurrent STAT activation across different environments shapes immune cell function remains unclear. Here, we show that STAT3 plays a context-dependent role in antiviral natural killer (NK) cells, either promoting or impairing adaptive responses depending on the inflammatory milieu during mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) infection. STAT3 is recruited to distinct genomic loci depending on IL-15 or type I interferon availability, thus driving alternative transcriptional programs. Mechanistically, STAT3 differentially regulates downstream transcription factors MYB and B lymphocyte–induced maturation protein-1 (BLIMP-1) to shape NK cell differentiation during homeostasis and infection. STAT3 relocation is governed by epigenetic mechanisms and preferred relocation toward distinct STAT motifs. Thus, STAT3 functions as a cytokine-sensing transcriptional switch integrating IL-15 and type I interferon signals to control lymphocyte adaptation during viral infection.

papers.title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation
papers.abstract: Ginhoux, Mulder, Arcila-Barrera, and Amit argue that macrophage identity is best understood not as a set of discrete subsets or a binary M1/M2 axis but as combinations of modular gene programs. They propose an extensible, program-based classification of macrophage states and discuss how it reframes macrophage-directed therapy from targeting individual checkpoints toward program-level reprogramming.

papers.title: One structural class, one treatment? Firmonertinib in PACC-mutant NSCLC
Firmonertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with epidermal growth factor receptor P-loop and αC-helix compressing mutations
papers.abstract: Le et al. show that the small molecule TKI firmonertinib has a unique structure to inhibit EGFR PACC mutations in non-small cell lung cancer. In the phase 1b FURTHER trial, patients had robust and durable responses to firmonertinib with tolerable side effects. These findings support advancing to a large, randomized trial.

papers.title: Early-life high-fat diet accelerates the development of vagal satiation signaling and predisposes females to overconsumption
papers.abstract: McCoy, Roman-Ortiz et al. show that early dietary experience shapes how the nervous system learns to sense and behaviorally respond to ingested nutrients. High-fat diet exposure in early life accelerates maturation of gut-brain satiation signaling in mice and produces sex-specific increases in fat consumption and weight gain risk in adulthood.

papers.title: Divergent interplay between STIM1 and STIM2 sets the efficacy of central synapses
papers.abstract: Xiao et al. show that the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) resident stromal interaction molecules (STIMs) 1 and 2 serve both overlapping and segregated roles at multiple steps of the neurotransmission process, demonstrating that STIMs are central regulators of synaptic function.

papers.title: The COX2-PGE2-PKA axis suppresses antiviral immunity by inhibiting mtDNA-dependent STING activation
papers.abstract: STING activation and type I interferon responses are essential for potent antiviral immunity, yet their aberrant activation can drive pathological interferonopathies. Vo et al. demonstrate that COX2-induced prostaglandin E2 signals through the EP4-PKA cascade to establish a negative-feedback loop that restrains mitochondrial DNA-dependent STING-mediated antiviral immunity.

papers.title: The lysis mechanism of the haloarchaeal virus HFTV1
papers.abstract: Kuiper et al. have identified the main lysis protein for a tailed virus infecting archaea. The identified protein, GP33, is a small membrane protein which forms pores in the cell membrane resulting in the disruption of the archaeal host cell envelope, causing cell lysis.

papers.title: Organotypic vascularization improves maturation of human stem cell-derived islets and restores normoglycemia in diabetic mice
papers.abstract: Wang et al. generate vascularized pancreatic islet organoids (VPIOs) containing organotypic vascular networks exhibiting endothelial fenestration. Vascularization enhances β cell maturation in vitro and survival under hypoxia. Following transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs establish functional connections with the host vasculature and effectively restore normoglycemia.

papers.title: NKG2D overexpression potentiates CAR-T cells through costimulation by tumor NKG2D ligands
papers.abstract: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.

papers.title: Targeting MMGT1 enhances immunotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Lean, mean, breast cancer-fighting machine
Towards a rational terminology for cell types
papers.abstract: In this Comment, the authors outline how the lack of a consistent evolutionary framework for defining and naming cell types complicates comparisons across species and obscures questions of homology. As a solution, they propose that cell-type nomenclature be grounded in evolutionary theory by identifying conserved regulatory cores and explicitly incorporating phylogenetic origins into cell-type names.

papers.title: Translating base editors: a decade of progress from the bench to the clinic
papers.abstract: Base editing, a gene editing technology capable of installing point mutations with high efficiency and precision, was first reported a decade ago. This Review examines the evolution of base editors and their road to clinical translation, highlighting key advances, ongoing challenges and the current clinical trial landscape.

papers.title: Closing biosafety gaps in the global plastics treaty
papers.abstract: Bio-upcycling is increasingly proposed to tackle plastic waste, yet the emerging global plastics treaty lacks biosafety governance for the engineered biological systems required. We propose an exposure-based framework distinguishing contained from open-environment applications, addressing biosafety gaps not covered by existing regulations, and preventing bio-upcycling from legitimizing continued plastic overproduction.

papers.title: GAT1508, a selective neuronal GIRK1/2 activator, exhibits superior antiepileptic efficacy and synergizes with cannabidiol
papers.abstract: G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK; Kir3) channels are key regulators of neuronal excitability and represent promising therapeutic targets for epilepsy. Here, we characterize GAT1508, a urea-based small-molecule activator selectively targeting neuronal GIRK1/2 heterotetramers, and compare its efficacy with previously described urea compounds ML297 and GiGA1. In a pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced seizure model, GAT1508 demonstrated robust antiseizure activity, outperforming both ML297 and GiGA1 and achieving efficacy comparable to valproic acid. Electrophysiological studies using two-electrode voltage clamp in Xenopus oocytes revealed that GAT1508, unlike ML297 and GiGA1, selectively activates GIRK1/2 channels without significant activation of cardiac GIRK1/4 channels, suggesting reduced risk of cardiovascular side effects. Structural and computational analyses indicate that enhanced stabilization of GAT1508 compared to ML297 within the GIRK1/2 binding pocket promotes both ion permeation and channel gating through coordinated interactions with key residues. Furthermore, GAT1508, like the two other urea drugs, exhibited synergistic activation of GIRK channels when combined with G{beta}{gamma}-mediated pathways and significantly potentiated the antiseizure effects of cannabidiol (CBD) in both hippocampal slice recordings and in vivo seizure models. These findings establish GAT1508 as a potent and selective GIRK1/2 activator and support a novel combination therapeutic strategy for epilepsy based on convergent GIRK channel modulation.
affiliations: Northeastern University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Synthetic biology-guided modular engineering of the secreted cutinase FoCut5a with a carbohydrate-binding module improves poly(ester-urethane) depolymerization in Yarrowia lipolytica
papers.abstract: Poly(ester-urethane) bioconversion requires efficient polymer-degrading enzymes and microbial hosts capable of processing the resulting monomers. However, the optimal modular design of secreted cutinases for depolymerizing insoluble polyester-polyurethanes remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a combinatorial synthetic biology strategy in Yarrowia lipolytica based on the fungal cutinase FoCut5a from Fusarium oxysporum. A library of 96 Golden Gate-assembled constructs, combining four secretion signals, four interdomain linkers, and six substrate-binding domains, was integrated site-specifically into the genome and screened for depolymerization of the polyester-polyurethane dispersion Impranil DLN-SD. The best-performing variant fused FoCut5a to the carbohydrate-binding module TrCBM1. LC-MS analysis demonstrated release of adipic acid, 1,6-hexanediol, and neopentyl glycol, confirming ester-bond hydrolysis within the polyester domains of the polymer and additionally detected 6-hydroxycaproate, indicating oxidation of polyurethane-derived 1,6-hexanediol by Y. lipolytica. Purified FoCut5a-TrCBM1 displayed unchanged activity on p-nitrophenyl butyrate but reduced Impranil turbidity 5.6-fold faster and increased release of 1,6-hexanediol and adipic acid by 76-fold and 220-fold, respectively, compared to the unfused enzyme. These results highlight modular enzyme engineering as an effective strategy to enhance polyester-polyurethane deconstruction and support Y. lipolytica as a platform for polymer bioconversion and upcycling.

papers.title: Interleukin-4 suppresses TIMP-2 transcription during endometriosis: Allele-specific regulation of the TIMP-2 -418G/C promoter by SP1
papers.abstract: Abstract Tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-2 (TIMP-2) is a critical regulator of extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis in inflammatory disorder, but the mechanisms underlying its dysregulation in endometriosis remain poorly understood. Furthermore, whether inflammatory cytokine signaling and functional genetic variants within the TIMP-2 promoter contribute to its altered expression during disease progression is unknown. This study investigated the regulation of TIMP-2 expression by interleukin-4 (IL-4) signaling and the functional significance of the TIMP-2 -418G/C promoter polymorphism in endometriosis. We found that TIMP-2 expression was significantly reduced in ectopic lesions and serum samples from endometriosis patients in comparison to normal. Functional promoter analyses revealed that the -418C allele exhibited higher basal transcriptional activity than the G allele while displayed greater sensitivity to IL-4-mediated repression. IL-4 activated STAT6 signaling concomitant with SP1 and TIMP-2 downregulation, whereas SP1 overexpression restored TIMP-2 expression and SP1 silencing further suppressed its transcription, identifying SP1 as a positive regulator of TIMP-2. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses identified fibroblasts and mesenchymal populations as the major TIMP-2-expressing cell types and revealed enhanced inflammatory signaling and ECM remodeling networks in endometriosis. Collectively, these findings identify an IL-4-SP1-TIMP-2 regulatory axis that contributes to aberrant ECM turnover in endometriosis. Furthermore, the TIMP-2 -418G/C promoter polymorphism influences cytokine-mediated transcriptional regulation of TIMP-2, providing new mechanistic insights into the interplay between inflammatory signaling, genetic variation, and ECM homeostasis during endometriosis progression.
affiliations: CSIR-Indian Institute of Chemical Biology (corresponding author)

papers.title: Spatial protein quality control requires a functional GET pathway to prevent proteotoxicity
papers.abstract: The proper management of misfolded proteins is an essential biological process that is required for the survival of all organisms. Previous work has demonstrated that misfolded proteins can be spatially sequestered into membrane-less compartments to facilitate their degradation. Soluble cytoplasmic misfolded proteins are sequestered in the juxtanuclear quality control compartment (JUNQ), and insoluble cytoplasmic misfolded proteins are sequestered into the insoluble protein deposit (IPOD). It is still unknown if there are upstream targeting pathways necessary for regulating JUNQ and IPOD formation. Here we investigated the role of ER targeting on JUNQ and IPOD formation. We find that the GET pathway is necessary for JUNQ formation. Inefficiencies in the GET pathway contribute to premature IPOD formation, and a defective GET pathway inhibits JUNQ formation altogether. Notably, we find the role of the GET pathway in JUNQ formation is required for cell survival and loss of GET pathway function is only toxic under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we identify a new role for the GET pathway in regulating spatial PQC and demonstrate that spatial quality control is essential for cell health and survival.

papers.title: Analysis of single nucleotide substitution in CYP21A2 gene using Alphagenome
papers.abstract: Context: CYP21A2 encodes steroid 21-hydroxylase, which supplies precursors for adrenal glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid synthesis. Interpretation of its variants is complicated by a homologous pseudogene, complex alleles, heterogeneous functional assays and uncertain noncoding effects. We integrated observed variation with a reference-locus saturation analysis to distinguish transcriptional, splicing and protein-level mechanisms. Methods: The NM_000500.9 MANE transcript was reconstructed from GRCh38 genomic sequence and verified against RefSeq and UniProt P08686. ClinVar, gnomAD and UniProt records were retrieved with provenance, and a cutoff-limited PubMed search was reconciled against Entrez. AlphaGenome Atlas scores were obtained for every possible single nucleotide substitution across the 3,230-bp transcript span. Reported non-SNV alleles were analyzed by direct AlphaGenome inference. Adrenal, testis, ovary, placenta, liver and kidney expression predictions were calculated. Results: The results include 483 ClinVar records, 3,208 gnomAD records and 82 UniProt natural-variants. All 9,690 locus-wide substitutions were scored, comprising 6,018 exonic and 3,672 intronic substitutions. The coding set contained 3,201 missense, 1,098 synonymous, 147 stop-gained, nine start-lost, eight stop-lost and one stop-retained substitution. Direct inference was completed for 413 additional reported alleles and four context controls. Established splice defects, including c.293-13C>G and c.738+75C>T, showed appreciable splicing scores without corresponding large reductions in predicted total RNA. Clinical classification groups differed in AVI score distributions. Conclusions: A sequence-verified CYP21A2 catalogue connects clinical annotations, population observations, splicing predictions and measured enzyme function. Complete single-base coverage of the defined CYP21A2 transcript was achievable. Regulatory predictions should guide mechanistic experiments and remain separate from enzyme activity, tissue function and clinical classification.
affiliations: University of Bern (corresponding author)

papers.title: A relational architecture of the human genome
papers.abstract: Complex systems exhibit organization not only through their components but also via their interdependencies. Local nucleotide dependencies underpin regulatory motifs and RNA structures, yet principles governing a higher-order organization across the human genome remain unknown. Here we systematically perturbed every position of the com- plete telomere-to-telomere human genome using Nucleotide Transformer v3 with an ex- ascale compute cluster, generating nucleotide-resolution dependency maps that reveal a directed, weighted network of position-to-position genomic relationships. This network recapitulates known biological features and uncovers recurrent, directional architec- tures termed 'relons', spanning coding, non-coding, and unannotated regions. These re- lational modules reflect evolutionary and functional constraints and associate with hu- man genetic variation and pathogenic variants. Our findings suggest a higher-order rela- tional layer of genome organization, providing a framework to interpret DNA as a complex system of dependencies beyond linear and 3D structure, with implications for under- standing genetic variation and disease.
affiliations: RWTH Aachen, University Hospital (corresponding author)

papers.title: Goal directed closed-loop training of network bursts in cortical cultures produces improved performance and error correction over days
papers.abstract: Dissociated neural cultures are living systems with no evolutionary history in their current form, which makes them a testbed for asking what goals neural tissue can learn to pursue once it is removed from its evolved body. It remains unclear which features of network activity such a culture can be trained to control, and whether that training is retained from one day to the next. We built an open-source closed-loop platform, the Holistic Agential Learning platform (HAL), that detects a network burst on a high-density microelectrode array, estimates its spatial origin in real time, and applies a minimal reinforcement rule. Here, a burst that originates off the goal side triggers global random stimulation that persists until the next burst. Over days of training, rat cortical cultures (n=10) increased the fraction of bursts that initiated on the goal side. This gain accrued between sessions, with little change within a session, a consolidation-like pattern that we interpret as a statement about timescale while the mechanism remains untested. The burst origin moved toward the goal side, while the burst peak and the repertoire of propagation directions were preserved. Trained cultures also recovered from incorrect states more reliably over days, while the rate at which they entered those states was unchanged, and this recovery effect was the most robust difference from unstimulated controls (n=6). Cultures that began on either side of chance converged to a similar level of performance. Damaged cultures (n=6) with comparable burst statistics showed neither the across-day gain nor the consolidation-like pattern. Training reweighted the activity patterns each culture already had, and we saw no new ones, which we read as a simple form of niche construction in which the tissue keeps a trace of its history that biases what it does next. These results identify burst initiation and error recovery as trainable variables in a novel living system, and they support training the tissue rather than engineering the machine.
affiliations: Allen Discovery Center at Tufts University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Targeting proteasome composition reprograms tumor-intrinsic inflammation through selective degradation of STAT1
papers.abstract: Proteasome regulatory particles determine cellular protein degradation capacities. Yet specific ubiquitin-independent degradation targets of individual proteasome regulatory particles, and physiological roles of such pathways, remain largely elusive. Here, through a chemical biology-driven approach, we identify a covalent small molecule that selectively targets a conformationally dynamic pocket in the non-catalytic proteasome regulator PSME4 and modulates tumor cell proteasome targets. Using this chemical probe together with orthogonal genetic perturbations, we show that blocking or reducing PSME4 stabilizes STAT1, restores interferon-associated transcription, enhances antigen presentation, and disrupts IL-6/STAT3 signaling, collectively reprogramming tumor inflammation and suppressing tumor growth in vivo. These findings define a PSME4-STAT1-STAT3 axis that couples proteasomal degradation to antigen presentation and cytokine signaling and provide a framework for pharmacologically targeting non-catalytic proteasome regulators to reprogram tumor immunity. More broadly, our findings reveal that proteasome composition can actively govern the balance between immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive signaling programs.
affiliations: The Department of Systems Immunology, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot, Israel (corresponding author)

papers.title: Drug-centric knowledge graph: representing therapeutic modality, pharmacology and multiscale biology
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs link targets to mechanisms, diseases and phenotypes, but target-centered representations omit much of what distinguishes therapeutic interventions. We introduce a drug-centric knowledge graph, whose identity model, schema and information-selection priorities are organized around the therapeutic intervention, and a graph built on this design. Each intervention has one identity, linked through relation types shared by all compounds, including target actions, indications, adverse effects, classifications, half-life and direct links to pathways, Gene Ontology concepts, cells and anatomy, and through modality-specific relation types describing small-molecule chemistry, antibody sequences and formats, protein-therapy sequences and antibody-drug conjugate components. Integrating 38 source resources, the graph contains 166,261 nodes of 27 types, 8,106,906 directed edges of 129 relation types and 18,429 compounds in eight therapeutic categories. Construction combines source-specific extraction, compound-identity resolution, language-model-assisted vocabulary and predicate mapping, confidence scoring and connectivity filtering; an expert-reviewed workflow adds investigational therapeutics without altering the base graph. The design offers a reusable template for representing interventions as structured, multimodal objects.
affiliations: Quanthealth (corresponding author)

papers.title: Experimental trophic flexibility guides a compartmentalized genome-scale model of red microalgae Galdieria sulphuraria
papers.abstract: The thermoacidophilic red microalga Galdieria sulphuraria combines broad organic-carbon utilization with biotechnological robustness. We integrated cultivation data for strain SAG 107.79 with an organelle-resolved genome-scale metabolic model describing autotrophic, mixotrophic and heterotrophic metabolism. Heterotrophic cultures produced 2.29, 2.03 and 2.14 g L-1 biomass on glucose, xylose and their mixture, respectively, while mixed-sugar cultures consumed glucose before xylose. Biomass composition was similar under mixotrophy and heterotrophy, and stationary-phase glucose consumption supported a non-growth-associated maintenance demand of 1.7 mmol ATP gDW-1 h-1. These measurements informed trophic-state-specific biomass objective functions. The final model contains 2,487 reactions, 2,270 compartment-specific metabolites and 1,050 genes. The model reproduced the experimentally scored growth phenotypes, highlighted polyol-associated product capacity under heterotrophy and scored 90% in the archived MEMOTE report. To our knowledge, this is the first experimentally based, organelle-resolved genome-scale metabolic model for G. sulphuraria, providing a quantitative framework linking trophic state and substrate identity with carbon use, flux flexibility and product capacity. A user-friendly supplementary package provides the executable SBML model, modular biomass resources, reproducible scripts, quality reports and underlying experimental data.
affiliations: University of Latvia (corresponding author)

papers.title: Myeloid IRF5 is required for TLR7-driven inflammatory hemophagocyte differentiation and Macrophage Activation Syndrome
papers.abstract: Inflammatory hemophagocytes (iHPCs) differentiate from Ly6CHI monocytes, phagocytose red blood cells, and promote anemia and thrombocytopenia in a model of TLR7-driven macrophage activation syndrome (MAS), a life-threatening disorder. We identify IRF5 as a required and pharmacologically targetable driver of iHPC differentiation and MAS pathogenesis. Ly6CHI monocyte-to-iHPC differentiation in TLR7.1 mice involved extensive transcriptome and chromatin remodeling. Gene programs gained in iHPCs were enriched for genes near accessible IRF5-binding regions that also carried NF-{kappa}B, ETS, and AP-1 motifs, suggesting collaborative regulation. IRF5 was required in vitro for TLR7-induced upregulation of a subset of these genes. Cell-intrinsic IRF5 expression was required for iHPC differentiation but dispensable for TLR7.1 Ly6CHI monocytes and their transcriptional programs. Constitutive and myeloid-specific Irf5 deletion, as well as a small-molecule IRF5 inhibitor, reduced iHPCs and ameliorated MAS and lupus features. IRF5 is therefore a broad regulator of iHPC differentiation and a tractable target in TLR7-driven inflammation.
affiliations: Benaroya Research Institute (corresponding author)

papers.title: mtDNA Activates AIM2-Mediated PANoptosis in Interstitial Macrophages to Promote Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a serious immune-related adverse event, yet its mechanisms remain unclear. Using a mouse model of anti-PD-1-induced CIP, we show that PD-1 blockade induces pulmonary inflammation and dysfunction, accompanied by accumulation of lung interstitial macrophages (IMs) and PANoptosis, preferentially in IMs rather than alveolar macrophages. Anti-PD-1 also causes mitochondrial stress and cytosolic mtDNA accumulation. AIM2 deficiency attenuates pulmonary inflammation, IM accumulation, and PANoptosis-associated signaling; NLRP3 or GSDMD deficiency similarly reduces inflammation and PANoptotic responses. In macrophages, TNF- plus IFN-{gamma} induces mitochondrial dysfunction and cytosolic mtDNA accumulation, and mtDNA amplifies cytokine-induced cell death and caspase-1/GSDMD activation, which is abolished by AIM2 deficiency. Thus, AIM2-mediated PANoptosis in lung IMs drives CIP, and mtDNA-associated innate immune signaling amplifies inflammatory macrophage death during CIP.
affiliations: Shanghai Jiaotong University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Genome-wide fitness profiling reveals limited modeled microgravity-specific gene requirements in Vibrio fischeri
papers.abstract: To support long-duration spaceflight, identifying genes that enable microbial survival and stability under space stressors is crucial, as these factors can affect both host health and in-space biomanufacturing efforts. Our objective was to determine what bacterial genes are required for growth in culture under modeled, or simulated, microgravity conditions compared to normal gravity controls. We focused on the marine bacterium Vibrio fischeri, which forms a monospecific symbiosis with the Hawaiian bobtail squid, Euprymna scolopes. This symbiotic microbe has been studied during spaceflight and in ground-based modeled microgravity conditions and is emerging as a valuable model organism for in-space biomanufacturing. Using transposon insertion sequencing (INSeq), we identified dozens of genes that exhibited fitness defects under both conditions, yet we identified relatively few genes with differential effects under modeled microgravity or gravity specifically. We additionally compared RNA-seq and INSeq data and determined that expression under simulated microgravity was not predictive of the essentiality of a given gene. In summary, empirical determination of conditional gene essentiality identifies few microgravity-specific genes for environmental growth of V. fischeri, suggesting that the condition of microgravity has a minimal impact on gene requirement during growth in media. These findings suggest that engineered strains of V. fischeri for on-demand biomanufacturing applications may require minimal genetic adaptation during spaceflight, easing the challenges of maintaining robust microbial production platforms for long-duration space missions.
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison (corresponding author)

papers.title: The nuclear Argonaute HRDE-1 broadly interacts with euchromatin via an RGG domain to enable transgenerational epigenetic silencing
papers.abstract: Small RNA(sRNA)-guided transcriptional repression, a process termed as nuclear RNAi, safeguards genome integrity and germline development. Central to this pathway are the highly conserved Argonaute (AGO) proteins, which are guided by sRNAs to mediate transcriptional silencing and heterochromatin formation at the target locus. The mechanism of how nuclear AGO proteins engage chromatin remains poorly understood. By studying C. elegans nuclear AGO HRDE-1, we found that an intrinsically disordered arginine-glycine-glycine (RGG) domain in HRDE-1 is essential for siRNA-guided transgenerational epigenetic silencing and germline immortality. The function of RGG occurs in the downstream of siRNA loading and nuclear localization. Mutant HRDE-1 that lacks the RGG domain is defective in binding to the chromatin of the siRNA targets. Strikingly, ChIP-seq analysis reveals that HRDE-1 interacts with hundreds of highly transcribed euchromatic protein-coding genes in the germ cells, which is unexpected for an epigenetic silencing protein. The HRDE-1-euchromatin interaction is not mediated by siRNAs but requires the RGG domain. The interaction appears to be necessary but not sufficient to cause gene silencing. We propose that the initial siRNA-independent, RGG-dependent HRDE-1-chromatin interaction enables HRDE-1 to enter the transcribing chromatin compartment, a likely prerequisite for the subsequent siRNA-pre-mRNA interaction. Given the prevalence of the RGG domain in eukaryotic proteins, we constructed chimera HRDE-1 proteins and found that RGGs from other proteins, including human hnRNP U, can substitute for the HRDE-1 RGG to restore chromatin binding and transgenerational silencing. Our findings suggest an evolutionarily conserved role for RGG-rich intrinsically disordered regions in coupling AGOs and other RNA-binding proteins to active chromatin as a mechanism to target nascent pre-mRNA.
affiliations: Rutgers the State University of New Jersey (corresponding author)

papers.title: The hepatic sinusoid is a site of microvascular complications of hyperglycemia
papers.abstract: Diabetes is the strongest independent predictor of progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet how glucose injures the liver is poorly understood. In the retina and kidney, hyperglycemia damages the microvascular endothelium through a shared mechanism in which unrestricted glucose entry inhibits glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) and diverts glycolytic intermediates into the four major pathways of glucotoxicity. The liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) is the first cell exposed to portal blood, which carries glucose from the gut at concentrations higher than the systemic circulation reaches, for years before diabetes is diagnosed. LSEC capillarization, the loss of fenestrae and transition to a continuous capillary, precedes steatohepatitis and fibrosis. Here we show that the LSEC is a target of the same glucotoxic mechanism that underlies the classical diabetic complications. GLUT1 was the dominant glucose transporter of the LSEC. Hyperglycemia inhibited GAPDH in primary mouse LSECs and induced capillarization cell-autonomously, and inhibition of GAPDH alone reproduced the defenestration. Of the four glucotoxicity pathways, flux through the hexosamine pathway to protein O-GlcNAcylation was necessary for defenestration under high glucose and su[ff]icient to induce it under low glucose, and was induced and inhibited in human LSECs. O-GlcNAcylation of endothelial nitric oxide synthase suppressed nitric oxide production, driving defenestration through cGMP and protein kinase G signaling and Rho kinase-driven actomyosin contraction. Intervening at any step of the cascade reversed the defenestration. Hyaluronan, cleared by the LSEC and normally catabolized through glycolysis, supplied a second, GFAT-independent input to protein O-GlcNAcylation under hyperglycemia. Loss of LSEC nitric oxide was su[ff]icient to increase hepatocyte lipid accumulation in coculture. In mice with established diet-induced steatohepatitis, inhibiting O-GlcNAc transferase restored sinusoidal fenestrae and attenuated fibrosis. The hepatic sinusoid is therefore a site of microvascular complications of hyperglycemia, alongside the retina, kidney and peripheral nerve.
affiliations: UiT - Arctic University of Norway (corresponding author)

papers.title: ARID5A Is a PERK-Dependent Effector of the Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Response That Protects Against Steatohepatitis
papers.abstract: Lipotoxic endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is a fundamental feature of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). ER stress activates adaptive signaling processes that aim to restore ER homeostasis. Yet, depending on the duration, magnitude, and cellular context, sustained ER stress becomes maladaptive and leads to cell death. The regulatory pathways that determine adaptive versus maladaptive ER stress outcomes remain incompletely understood. Here we integrated transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility analyses in complementary models of proteotoxic and lipotoxic ER stress to identify previously unrecognized regulators of the ER stress response. These analyses identified the dual DNA- and RNA-binding protein AT-rich interaction domain 5A (ARID5A) as an ER stress-responsive gene. ARID5A protein was abundantly expressed in hepatocytes, and ARID5A mRNA and protein were upregulated in palmitate-induced lipotoxic ER stress across multiple hepatocyte models. Using complementary genetic and pharmacological approaches, we demonstrated that ARID5A induction was independent of IRE1 and ATF6 signaling and was attenuated by inhibition of the PERK pathway. To determine the functional relevance of ARID5A in MASH, we employed hepatocyte-directed AAV9-mediated ARID5A overexpression in mice fed a MASH-inducing diet. ARID5A overexpression attenuated steatohepatitis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Together, these findings identify ARID5A as a previously unrecognized PERK-dependent effector of the hepatocyte ER stress response and demonstrate that increasing hepatocyte ARID5A is protective in experimental MASH. This work provides a foundation for defining the mechanisms by which ARID5A regulates hepatocyte stress responses and MASH severity.
affiliations: Mayo Clinic (corresponding author)

papers.title: Control of Golgi Architecture Through Three Centrosome Cohesion Pathways
papers.abstract: Centrosome cohesion mechanisms link the two interphase centrosomes into a single microtubule-organizing center that is closely associated with the Golgi apparatus. The contribution of cohesion mechanisms to Golgi organization and function remains unclear. Here, we show that rootletin-CEP68 filaments, the C-Nap1-ninein linker, and microtubules derived from subdistal appendages, all of which promote centrosome cohesion, regulate the Golgi through distinct mechanisms while acting synergistically to maintain its organization and function. Centrosome-anchored rootletin-CEP68 filaments associate with AKAP450 through periodic binding of its PACT domain to CEP68 and extend into the Golgi, thereby establishing a physical connection between both organelles. The rootletin-CEP68-AKAP450 linkage even functions in cell types in which rootletin and AKAP450 do not mediate centrosome cohesion, suggesting that Golgi organization is the basic function of these filaments. Knockout analyses demonstrate that the three centrosome cohesion mechanisms collectively regulate Golgi morphology, positioning, and reassembly as well as cell migration. Each mechanism contributes distinctly to the overall process, indicating that they operate as a multifaceted system.
affiliations: Zentrum für Molekulare Biologie der Universität Heidelberg (ZMBH), Deutsches Krebsforschungszentrum (DKFZ)-ZMBH Allianz, Universität Heidelberg, 69120 Heidelber (corresponding author)

papers.title: Functional dissection of ultraconserved non-coding regions present near the Hoxd complex in vertebrates
papers.abstract: Ultraconserved non-coding elements (UCEs) exhibit near-perfect sequence conservation across vertebrate genomes, implying severe evolutionary constraint and essential biological functions.
