Here, we systematically disentangle how air-liquid interface (ALI), extracellular matrix (ECM) cues and dimensionality interact to regulate tumor epithelial states. Using five architectural configurations, we demonstrate that these parameters act synergistically to promote distinct morphological, transcriptional and inflammatory phenotypes not observed under conventional 2D or submerged 3D cultures. ALI broadly enhanced epithelial cohesion, progenitor activation, partial EMT programs and cytokine expression, whereas ECM embedding further induced ALI-mediated mesenchymal activation, matrix remodeling and invasive cytoskeletal organization. Notably, 3D ALI uniquely produced a hybrid alveolar-mucinous phenotype characterized by concurrent SP-C and MUC5B induction, alongside integrated epithelial, basal and mucosecretory identities. These emergent states reflect tumor-relevant plasticity and illuminate architectural controls over lineage infidelity, invasion and inflammatory activation. Together, these findings establish ALI-ECM-dimensionality intersections as critical regulators of lung tumor phenotype and provides a systematic architectural framework for designing more physiologically relevant in vitro lung cancer models.
affiliations: Koc University (corresponding author)

papers.title: The eIF3a subunit drives RNA binding within the eIF3 complex
papers.abstract: Eukaryotic initiation factor 3 (eIF3) is a multi-subunit protein complex that binds the 40S pre-initiation complex (PIC) and has an essential role in messenger RNA (mRNA) recruitment, a process encompassing mRNA attachment and loading, scanning, and start-codon recognition. During recruitment, eIF3 is positioned to contact both the 18S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) component of the PIC and the mRNA, but how individual eIF3 subunits contribute to these RNA interactions remains poorly understood. A major obstacle has been the lack of a compositionally defined, biochemically active reconstituted yeast eIF3 complex that enables systematic analysis of individual subunits and defined subcomplexes. Here, we reconstitute Saccharomyces cerevisiae eIF3 from individually purified recombinant subunits and show that it is compositionally stable under our assay conditions and recapitulates core biochemical activities of native eIF3, including PIC binding, stimulation of capped mRNA recruitment, and RNA binding. Using this system, we show that eIF3a provides a core RNA-binding activity within eIF3 and that interactions with other eIF3 subunits modulate this activity in the intact complex and in defined eIF3a-containing subcomplexes. These results establish a reconstituted yeast eIF3 system for dissecting subunit-level biochemical activities and support a model in which subunit context tunes eIF3a-driven RNA binding during initiation.
affiliations: Vassar College (corresponding author)

papers.title: Giant Vesicle Platform for Synthetic Endoplasmic Reticulum Networks
papers.abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a membrane-bound organelle found in all eukaryotic cells. This organelle has a fascinating morphology, which involves a network of membrane nanotubes and three-way junctions connecting three nanotubes. Previous reconstitution studies were based on proteo-liposomes with a size of 100 to 200 nanometers, using electron microscopy as the main method to image the resulting membrane morphologies. These studies revealed the importance of membrane GTPases, that is, membrane proteins that hydrolyse GTP. Here, we introduce an alternative platform for the formation of synthetic ER networks starting from giant unilamellar vesicles with a typical size of 10 mirometers and containing a single membrane GTPase such as atlastin from fruit flies or Sey1 from yeast. This giant vesicle approach makes the networks accessible to optical microscopy, by which one can elucidate both their structure and their dynamics. We first demonstrate that the membranes' propensity to form synthetic ER networks depends strongly on the lipid composition. More precisely, we show that this propensity varies non-monotonically with the mole fraction of cholesterol and that the frequency of three-way junctions has a maximum for an optimal mole fraction between 10 and 15 mol%. This optimal value is comparable to the mole fraction of cholesterol as estimated for ER membranes in vivo. We also demonstrate the formation of synthetic ER networks when the membranes contain only the membrane GTPase Sey1 but no other membrane protein, which implies that Sey1 is able on its own to generate a high membrane curvature. Based on the reconstitution approach introduced here, the synthetic ER networks can now be further investigated using the versatile toolbox that has been developed for giant vesicles.
affiliations: Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces (corresponding author)

papers.title: When can site-specific glycoform compositions resolve biosynthetic rates?
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry measures site-specific glycoform compositions, but when these measurements can resolve upstream biosynthetic rates remains unclear. We assess whether small changes in effective rates, each representing the processing capacity of a group of biosynthetic reactions, can be distinguished near specified baseline rates with secretion held fixed. Because proportions sum to one, m jointly normalised glycoform classes provide at most m-1 independent quantities. Distinguishing changes in k rates therefore requires at least k+1 classes, although this count alone does not ensure identifiability. In a canonical N-glycan network with eight rates, exhaustive evaluation of nine-class panels identified panels that could locally distinguish all eight rates. Among these panels, class choice changed the allowable measurement error by approximately 18-fold for the same target uncertainty in inferred rates. A separate simulation within the fixed network showed that estimating rate-change combinations with weaker composition responses reduced bias but amplified measurement noise. We applied the framework to plasma data from 40 controls and 70 patients across 14 inherited glycosylation-disorder groups. A prespecified composition score for the expected pathway disturbance ranked among the top two in 13 of 14 groups. Network responses linked observed composition shifts to biosynthetic reaction classes. Expanding site models from five to eight reaction classes improved control-composition fit but reduced the number of sites at which all modelled rates were locally distinguishable and increased noise sensitivity. Rate inference thus requires sufficient panel size, separable rate responses, adequate measurement precision and a model that fits the composition. These requirements guide measurement design and help determine whether compositions support pathway-level interpretation or individual-rate inference.
affiliations: Nagoya University: Nagoya Daigaku (corresponding author)

papers.title: An epigenetic palimpsest: the King penguin's blood methylome reveals conserved hematopoietic ageing
papers.abstract: Age-associated DNA methylation is conserved across vertebrates, but whether epigenetic ageing reflects cellular ageing programmes or age-dependent shifts in cell composition remains unresolved. Here, using 126 whole-blood methylomes from known-age King penguins (Aptenodytes patagonicus), we exploit a vertebrate system in which nucleated erythrocytes dominate peripheral blood, minimizing the influence of leukocyte heterogeneity. We identify a core set of 409 ageing-associated genes showing lifelong, clock-like methylation change. These genes are strongly enriched for regulators of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) function and niche communication. Integration of methylome, transcriptome and chromatin-accessibility data reveals that many of the strongest ageing signals derive from genes inactive in mature erythrocytes, consistent with the persistence of epigenetic states from ancestral hematopoietic progenitors. A comparison with methylation profiles from 1,501 humans identified a conserved cross-species subset of ageing genes, and a human epigenetic age model constructed solely from orthologues of penguin ageing genes predicts chronological age with high accuracy while remaining largely insensitive to blood cell composition. We propose that blood epigenetic ageing signatures contain a long-lived cellular memory of stem-cell ageing, that may represent an evolutionarily ancient layer of the vertebrate ageing process.
affiliations: University of Helsinki (corresponding author)

papers.title: PRC2-binding regions are hotspots of DNA methylation entropy in pre-cancer and cancer
papers.abstract: DNA methylation aberrations and variability are pervasive features of cancer, yet their relationship with chromatin regulation remains incompletely understood. Across hundreds of matched tumor-normal methylomes, regions with the highest methylation entropy in both tumor and normal tissues were consistently enriched for PRC2-associated factors. In tumors, inter-sample methylation variability was increased across the full range of PRC2-associated levels, while mean methylation progressively increased from low- to high-PRC2-binding regions; this gradient was substantially weaker in matched normal tissues. PRC2-associated regions with higher DNA methylation levels were preferentially associated with poised and repressed chromatin states, reduced chromatin accessibility, and reduced gene expression. Independent normal-precancer-cancer cohorts showed that this PRC2-associated methylation state emerges early, with precancerous and malignant tissues displaying highly similar profiles that are distinct from those of healthy tissues. Single-cell colon cancer methylomes independently confirmed increased methylation entropy at PRC2 regions. Higher PRC2-region entropy was associated with scores reflecting hypoxic states, aggressive tumor features, and poorer survival outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify PRC2-binding regions as hotspots of DNA methylation variability that become dysregulated during tumorigenesis.
affiliations: Fingerprint Diagnostics (corresponding author)

papers.title: TBX3 is required for the differentiation of a subset of retinal ganglion and cone photoreceptor cells
papers.abstract: Retinogenesis is a key step driving the formation of the neurons that later coordinate angiogenesis in the retina. Understanding these complex interactions requires dissecting apart its cellular and molecular drivers. To tease apart the molecular links coupling retinogenesis to vascular development, we utilized conditional knockout mouse models to selectively delete the transcription factor T-box 3 (Tbx3) in 1) astrocytes, 2) postnatal retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), or 3) retinal progenitors. We demonstrate that the hypovascular retina phenotype observed upon Tbx3 loss most likely stems from a disruption of early retinogenesis. Embryonic analyses revealed that TBX3 is required during a critical retinogenic window coinciding with ATOH7 activity. While ATOH7+ progenitors are more abundant in Tbx3 mutants, the expression of key RGC and cone precursor factors (including TBX5, RXRgamma, ISL1/2, POU4F2, SHH, LHX4 and OTX2) is severely diminished, halting proper RGC and cone differentiation. Utilizing birthdating experiments and developmental immunostaining, we establish TBX3 as a novel upstream regulator of RGC and cone photoreceptor specification. Because the degeneration of RGCs is the definitive hallmark of diseases like glaucoma, identifying TBX3 as a driver of early RGC formation positions it as a promising new candidate biomarker for early-stage glaucoma diagnosis and potentially therapeutic targeting.
affiliations: Upstate Medical University (corresponding author)

papers.title: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control post-transcriptional gene expression by regulating RNA processing, localization, stability, and translation. However, our understanding of RNA regulation remains limited by the resolution, scale, and uniformity of available RBP binding maps. Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles. We applied ecCLIP to 67 endogenously tagged RBPs in HEK293T cells, generating a high-quality transcriptome-scale atlas that recovered known binding preferences and captured post-transcriptional regulons linked to RNA half-life. To test the utility of the atlas, we incorporated ecCLIP into Borzuki, a Borzoi-derived sequence-to-function model trained on complementary RNA degradation, expression, CLIP, and Perturb-seq data. Inclusion of ecCLIP data improved RNA half-life prediction and assessment of 3' UTR variant effects on RNA stability, demonstrating that our atlas helps capture RNA dynamics. To directly model the cis-regulatory grammar underlying these RBP-RNA interactions, we developed Pythia, a structure-aware neural network architecture that incorporates context-free grammar-inspired fixed convolutions to explicitly encode RNA base-pairing features. Pythia predicted RBP binding from sequence and structural context and decomposed predictions into sequence- and structure-dependent components. We tested this decomposition for five RBPs using massively parallel reporter CLIP (MPRC) binding assays in cells, using synthetic RNA libraries containing mutations designed to preserve or disrupt predicted RNA structures across nominated binding sites. We used the same MPRC strategy to confirm allele-specific binding effects for variants prioritized by Pythia. Together, ecCLIP and Pythia provide a resource for structure-aware decoding of RNA-protein interaction grammar and interpretation of post-transcriptional regulatory variation.
affiliations: Arc Institute, University of California, San Francisco (corresponding author)

papers.title: Cooperative IDR-folded domain interplay governs HP1α phase separation and underlies biphasic regulation by pathogenic poly-PR
papers.abstract: HP1 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), yet the prevailing model, which attributes condensation almost entirely to intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), leaves the role of its folded domains unresolved. Using solution and solid-state NMR, we show that HP1 LLPS is instead governed by reciprocal interplay between IDRs and folded domains. Within the condensed phase, solid-state NMR reveals a dynamic hierarchy: the chromoshadow domain (CSD) assembles into polymorphic oligomers that form rigid cores, while the phosphorylation sites on the N-terminal extension (NTE) remain highly mobile, challenging their proposed role as stable multivalent hubs. Phosphorylation of the NTE instead promotes LLPS primarily by increasing local rigidity and releasing the NTE from the chromodomain (CD) to relieve autoinhibition, with electrostatic charge contributing secondarily. The C-terminal extension (CTE) suppresses phase separation through two routes: weakening the association between the hinge region (HR) and the CSD, and inhibiting interactions between CSD dimers. ALS-associated poly-PR targets this network at the NTE and exerts concentration-dependent biphasic regulation, promoting LLPS at low concentrations via multivalent bridging and dissolving condensates at high concentrations via saturation, a switch recapitulated in cells and in mouse brain. These findings reframe HP1 condensation from an IDR-driven process to one cooperatively governed by IDR-folded domain interplay.
affiliations: MOE Key Laboratory for Cellular Dynamics, School of Life Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China (corresponding author)

papers.title: Decoupling of CO2 and O2 fluxes reveals oxygen-independent decarboxylation in anoxic mammalian cells
papers.abstract: Canonical understanding of cellular respiration holds that CO2 production tracks oxygen consumption, and mammalian cells deprived of oxygen are thought to rely on lactate fermentation, which yields no net CO2. Because standard respirometry infers CO2 flux either from oxygen consumption or from extracellular acidification rather than measuring it directly, a CO2 flux decoupled from oxygen would go undetected or be misattributed to glycolysis. Using direct measurement of CO2 and O2 fluxes from the gas phase in anoxic mammalian cells, we show that a substantial CO2 efflux persists after oxygen is fully removed. This anoxic flux scales linearly with normoxic CO2 and with cell mass, and exhibits a lower activation energy than normoxic respiration, suggesting a distinct rate-limiting chemistry. Pyruvate and -ketobutyrate increased the anoxic CO2 flux while lactate dehydrogenase inhibition abolished the pyruvate-induced increase, supporting a role for cytosolic NAD+ regeneration in oxygen-independent decarboxylation. 13C tracing identified a substantial glutamine-derived component, consistent with mitochondrial decarboxylation, and a smaller glucose-derived component associated with the cytosolic pentose phosphate pathway. Direct CO2 measurement thus reframes lactate dehydrogenase as an enabler of oxygen-independent decarboxylation.
affiliations: University of Tartu, Institute of Biomedicine and Translational Medicine, Department of Physiology (corresponding author)

papers.title: Chronic Electrophysiology Captures Progressive Variability in DNA-Damaged Cardiac Networks
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological recordings provide a key functional readout of cardiac health. Most in vitro studies rely on acute measurements rather than recording evolving functional changes. Here, we implement a microelectrode array (MEA) based system for chronic electrophysiological monitoring of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (iPSC-CM) monolayers. Electrophysiology recordings were maintained for up to 40 days, enabling longitudinal assessment of field potential amplitude, field potential duration, beat frequency, conduction velocity, and waveform morphology. Untreated iPSC-CM monolayers exhibited stable electrophysiological behavior throughout chronic culture. Following exposure to the cardiotoxic chemotherapeutic doxorubicin, chronic recordings captured progressive deterioration in electrical activity, including reduced field potential amplitude, altered repolarization dynamics, increased beat-to-beat variability, and reduced conduction that persisted after drug removal. Electrode-resolved analyses further revealed pronounced progressive spatial variability, highlighting localized responses that would be obscured by population-averaged measurements. Endpoint assays indicated reduced calcium transient amplitude and altered calcium reuptake, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and loss of connexin 43, findings consistent with the impaired electrical activity observed in chronic recordings. Together, these results establish chronic electrophysiological monitoring as a powerful approach for resolving the spatiotemporal progression of cardiotoxicity and other dynamic cardiac processes in vitro.
affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University (corresponding author)

papers.title: A Novel Computational Framework to Investigate the Biomechanics of Burrowing
papers.abstract: Head-first burrowing likely imposes strong mechanical demands on the skull of fossorial vertebrates, but how cranial tissues respond to these loads remains obscure. Here, we developed a computational framework integrating the discrete element method (DEM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to investigate cranial biomechanics during burrowing. We used Blanus cinereus, a round-headed amphisbaenian, as a model to establish DEM predictions that were validated and calibrated against in vitro experiments across three substrates and compared with in vivo push forces. DEM-calibrated particle contact forces were then transferred to an anatomically detailed finite element model to quantify cranial loading. The analyses suggested that soft tissues accommodated substantial deformation, while the skull transmitted burrowing loads from the premaxilla towards the occipital region. Cranial sutures further redistributed stresses and strains within the skull. This validated DEM-FEA framework links particle-scale substrate interactions with internal cranial biomechanics and provides a quantitative approach for investigating the mechanics of head-first burrowing across fossorial vertebrates.
affiliations: University College London (corresponding author)

papers.title: A multimodal foundation model to integrate histology with spatial molecular programs
papers.abstract: Histology and spatial transcriptomics provide complementary views of cancer morphology and molecular organization, yet their spatial correspondence has not been learned at scale. We developed SQUALL, a multimodal foundation model pretrained on histMol, comprising 1.93 billion spatially aligned histology-transcriptomics spots/bins from 3,446 sections across 33 tissues and 12 platforms. By learning spatial morphology-molecular correspondences, SQUALL enables virtual spatial transcriptomics, tumor microenvironment characterization, and molecularly informed histology representations for clinical prediction. SQUALL generalized virtual spatial gene expression profiling across cohorts, cancers, and platforms. Its representations resolve tumor microenvironments including progression-associated tumor trajectories in breast cancer and recurrence-associated immune-excluded regions in ovarian tumor, together with underlying transcriptional programs. Applied to whole-slide histology, SQUALL enabled outcome and treatment-response prediction while revealing interpretable features associated with risk. Together, these results establish large-scale spatially aligned histology-transcriptomics pretraining as a general framework for connecting tissue morphology, molecular programs, microenvironmental organization, and clinical phenotypes.
affiliations: Peking University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Spatially resolved tumor-microenvironment architecture defines therapeutic response in unresectable hepatoblastoma
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatoblastoma exhibits variable therapeutic response that is not fully explained by current risk stratification. While prior studies have characterized tumor composition, the role of spatial organization in determining outcome, particularly in unresectable disease requiring transplantation under immunosuppression, remains unclear. Methods: We integrated spatial transcriptomics using the 10x Genomics Visium platform (n = 11 tumors) with single-cell spatial molecular imaging using NanoString CosMx (n = 3 tumors) on post-chemotherapy explant specimens across clinically defined groups (relapse-prone unresectable, non-relapse unresectable, and resectable hepatoblastoma). Spatial deconvolution, module scoring, spatial co-localization, and cell-cell interaction analyses were used to define region-level transcriptional programs and their underlying cellular organization. Results: We identified three spatial architectures associated with clinical outcome. Relapse-prone tumors exhibited a centralized, TME-dominated organization enriched for progenitor-like, cycling, and stress-responsive tumor cell states co-localized with SPP1+ TAMs and CAFs, with enrichment of hypoxia response, extracellular matrix remodeling, and Midkine (MDK-LRP1) signaling. Non-relapse tumors displayed a distributed architecture with compartmentalized tumor-immune interactions, increased immune engagement, and preserved epithelial differentiation, including inflammatory hepatocyte-like states. Resection samples showed reduced tumor cell state heterogeneity and more uniform TME-immune organization. Conclusions: Integration of regional and single-cell spatial transcriptomics across two platforms reveals that the chemo-remodeled tumor architecture of hepatoblastoma encodes spatially organized tumor cell-TME interactions as central determinants of therapeutic response.
affiliations: UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh (corresponding author)

papers.title: Pan-cancer remodeling of reactive oxygen species homeostasis: distinct roles of the ROS-generation and antioxidant arms in immune context and outcome
papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are double-edged in cancer: tumor cells sustain high ROS generation while up-regulating antioxidant defense, so that the net balance between the two arms, rather than absolute ROS abundance, is the biologically meaningful quantity. Whether that balance defines a conserved tumor state across cancer types has been unclear. Here an experimentally measured ROS phenotype, obtained from a three-channel gold-nanocluster array, was generalized to public transcriptomes through a 107-gene ROS program scored in a large cell-line panel and in pan-cancer tumor and adjacent-normal tissue. The optical readout was reproducible and fully discriminative between cell lines, establishing the fingerprint as a quantitative starting point. In tumors, the generation and antioxidant arms were coordinately up-regulated relative to normal tissue, yet the two arms dissociated in their biology. The composite balance score tracked reduced immune infiltration consistently across cohorts, but arm-level decomposition showed that it was carried by low generation-arm activity in immune-cold tumors and followed arithmetically from how the balance score is defined; the association does not implicate antioxidant defense in immune infiltration. The clinical association pointed the other way: adverse outcome was attributable to the antioxidant arm, whereas generation was null. In cohort-held-out validation, tumors were separated from adjacent normal tissue, with redox programs outperforming generic phenotypic programs, indicating that the same program transfers across tumor types. Tumor remodeling of ROS homeostasis is therefore widespread, but its two arms carry distinct meanings: the balance score, driven by its generation term, reports immune context, whereas the antioxidant arm reports clinical risk.
affiliations: Anhui Medical University (corresponding author)

papers.title: More than just a passive brick in the wall: the nucleosome facilitates DNA polymerase β activity in linker DNA and its PARP-dependent regulation in the BER sub-pathway choice
papers.abstract: DNA polymerase {beta} (Pol{beta}) is a central player of base excision repair (BER), performing gap-filling synthesis on damaged DNA. While nucleosome core particles (NCPs) are known to impede activity of BER enzymes, the regulation of this process in linker DNA adjacent to nucleosomes remains unclear. Here we demonstrate an unexpected stimulation of Pol{beta}-catalyzed strand-displacement synthesis in linker DNA by the adjacent NCP. Notably, the nucleosome context reinforces the regulatory modulation of Pol{beta} activity by PARP1/PARP2 and FEN1. While linker histone H1 restricts strand-displacement synthesis at the nucleosome entry/exit site, PARP1 and PARP2 modulate Pol{beta} function through competitive binding to DNA gaps or nicks and via poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation (PARylation). At the same time, PARPs binding differentially regulates BER sub-pathway choice, and PARylation alleviates H1-mediated inhibition. These findings reveal a multi-layered regulatory system wherein the nucleosome acts as a dynamic platform coordinating Pol{beta} activity and its interplay with chromatin-associated factors, influencing the balance between short- and long-patch BER. The research advances understanding of chromatin-mediated control of BER DNA repair synthesis and the functional specialization of PARP1 and PARP2 in maintaining genome stability.
affiliations: Institute of Chemical Biology and Fundamental Medicine, SB RAS, Novosibirsk, Russia (corresponding author)

papers.title: A cell death-independent role for MLKL in TGF-β receptor recycling in Marfan syndrome
papers.abstract: Marfan syndrome (MFS) causes thoracic aortic aneurysm through mutations in the fibrillin-1 gene and subsequent dysregulated TGF-{beta} signalling. Mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) executes necroptosis after RIPK3-dependent phosphorylation, but also functions in endosomal trafficking. Here we show that MLKL phosphorylation sustains TGF-{beta} receptor recycling and aortic wall integrity without causing cell death. Phosphorylation-dead MLKLS345A/S347A (MlklAA) mice developed aortic root dilation with disorganised collagen architecture and a secretory-pathway proteomic signature. Crossing them with Fbn1C1039G/+ MFS mice aggravated aortic dilation, disrupted collagen fibril ultrastructure and prolyl/lysyl hydroxylation, and caused lethal rupture under angiotensin II. Complete MLKL deficiency reproduced this phenotype. Phosphorylated MLKL was increased in MFS aortas, yet cleaved caspase-3, TUNEL positivity, smooth muscle cell content and leukocyte infiltration were unchanged. In smooth muscle cells, MLKL depletion dysregulated collagen-modifying enzymes, altered TGF-{beta}-driven matrix remodelling and impaired RAB11-dependent TGF{beta}R1 recycling. These findings suggest that phosphorylation-dependent, non-lytic functions of MLKL may contribute to the maintenance of thoracic aortic integrity in MFS.
affiliations: Department III of Internal Medicine, Faculty of Medicine and University Hospital Cologne, University of Cologne, Cologne, Germany. (corresponding author)

papers.title: Ultrastructural Analysis of Extracellular Vesicles and Surface Protrusions from the Parasite Tritrichomonas foetus
authors: de Figueiredo, R. C. B. Q.
papers.abstract: Tritrichomonas foetus is an extracellular flagellated protist responsible for bovine and feline tritrichomonosis, yet several aspects of its cell biology and pathogenicity remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the presence of extracellular vesicles (EVs) and membrane protrusions in T. foetus using complementary electron microscopy and immunolabeling approaches. EV-like structures of different sizes were found protruding from the parasite cell body and anterior flagella, and ultrathin sections showed continuity between the membranes of these protrusions and the plasma or flagellar membrane. Multivesicular bodies containing intraluminal vesicles were also observed, and an EV-enriched fraction isolated from conditioned medium contained vesicles with a broad size distribution, consistent with heterogeneous EV populations. Immunofluorescence further showed tetraspanin-1 in intracellular vesicles, flagella, and vesicular structures protruding from the parasite surface. Exposure to bovine preputial epithelial cells resulted in a ninefold increase in the percentage of parasites displaying flagellar cytoneme-like structures, suggesting a possible role for these projections in host-parasite interactions. VPS32, a component of the ESCRT-III machinery, was found in intraluminal vesicles, vesicles protruding from the cell body and flagella, isolated EVs, and flagellar membrane protrusions. In parasites overexpressing VPS32, the number of vesicles per flagellum increased, and the percentage of cells with flagellar cytoneme-like projections was fivefold higher than in control parasites. Pearling-like protrusions containing VPS32 were also observed. Together, these findings provide ultrastructural evidence for heterogeneous EV populations associated with the cell body and flagella of T. foetus and suggest that VPS32 could contribute to flagellar EV and membrane protrusion formation.
affiliations: Fiocruz, Instituto Aggeu Magalhaes (corresponding author)

papers.title: Escape from replicative crisis and immortalization precedes complex genome evolution
papers.abstract: Shortening of telomeres restricts the proliferative capacity of human somatic cells by inducing replicative senescence and crisis. During cancerous transformation, premalignant cells must overcome these barriers and acquire replicative immortality. Single-cell DNA strand-specific genome sequencing of crisis cells revealed extreme genome instability characterized by complex chromosomal abnormalities. Unexpectedly, spontaneously emerging postcrisis clones showed relatively few and simple structural variants. However, with accumulating divisions following crisis escape, the genomes of immortal postcrisis clones evolve and amass genomic alterations, including tetraploidization events with subsequent losses and gains of individual chromosomes. Our data point towards a new model of tumorigenesis in which crisis acts as a strong selective barrier against cells with aberrant karyotypes, and in which high karyotypic complexity is acquired after immortalization and crisis escape.
affiliations: The Salk Institute for Biological Studies (corresponding author)

papers.title: Apical-Out Ileal Organoids: A Versatile Platform for Probing Gut-Nanomaterial Interactions
papers.abstract: The human ileal epithelium forms a critical interface governing interactions with luminal microorganisms and nanomaterials, yet physiologically relevant in vitro models with accessible apical surfaces remain limited. Here, human apical-out ileoids derived from healthy ileal biopsies are established as a platform that recapitulates the architecture and complexity of the native ileal epithelium. Assessment of donor- and passage-dependent variability identifies a representative ileoid line and a robust culture window. Integrated proteomic, imaging, ultrastructural, and functional analyses demonstrate preservation of key epithelial features, including brush-border organization, barrier integrity, absorptive capacity, and multiple endocytic pathways. Intact ileoids internalize nanoparticles of distinct surface charge, including empty lipid nanoparticles compositionally matched to approved mRNA vaccine formulations, establishing that uptake can be quantified across an unperturbed apical surface. This uptake is restrained by a retained mucin-rich glycocalyx. Cleavage of surface-attached mucins selectively enhances uptake of negatively charged nanoparticles, leaving near-neutral and positively charged nanoparticles unchanged, and increasing entry of Salmonella bacteria. These findings reveal the glycocalyx as a charge-selective regulator of epithelial uptake. In conclusion, our study provides a foundation for nanoparticle-epithelium investigations using human apical-out ileoids, and a versatile, translationally relevant platform for nanomedicine delivery, host-microbe interactions, and epithelial transport.
affiliations: Department of Pharmacy, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden (corresponding author)

papers.title: NanoPlasmiQC: Full plasmid sequencing with ONT long-reads and automatic data analysis
authors: de Oliveira, J. A. V. S.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing has shown a rapid technological development during the last years. It has been established as the standard method for the sequencing of plant genomes and has also gained importance for full plasmid sequencing. As Sanger sequencing has a limited read length of about 1 kb, long read sequencing offers a great advantage, as the full plasmid can be sequenced in one read. Here, we present a cost-effective workflow to sequence full plasmids and compare the results against an expectation. The per plasmid cost of this workflow is determined by the number of plasmids investigated simultaneously, but can be lower than the price of a single Sanger sequencing reaction. We developed a workflow for automatic data processing, which allows us to complete sequencing and data analysis within a day.
affiliations: University of Bonn, Institute for Cellular & Molecular Botany (IZMB) (corresponding author)

papers.title: A versatile set of computational tools for inference of genetic ancestry from human molecular data
papers.abstract: Molecular properties of human diseases and conditions often exhibit dependence on the genetic ancestry of the donor. In order to make more human molecular data available for ancestry-informed research, we developed a set of software tools termed Robust Ancestry Inference using Data Synthesis (RAIDS) for inference of genetic ancestry from sequence data that pose challenges to genotyping. Here we describe a recent expansion and refinement of RAIDS, applicable to nucleic-acid sequence data resultant from a broad range of experimental strategies. These strategies currently include whole-genome, whole-exome, and targeted gene panel sequencing, RNA-Seq, including single-cell RNA-Seq, chromatin-accessibility (ATAC-Seq), and protein-binding (ChIP-Seq) assays. RAIDS inferential tools perform robustly in the presence of somatic nucleic-acid alterations caused by cancer and under the conditions of extreme non-uniformity of sequence read coverage, yielding both global ancestry and ancestral admixtures of the donor. RAIDS is available as an eponymous Bioconductor package.
affiliations: CSHL (corresponding author)

papers.title: From Ligand Binding to Pore Opening in the Mosquito Odorant Receptor AaegOR10
papers.abstract: Mosquito olfaction is central to host seeking and other behaviors relevant to vector ecology and disease transmission. Mosquito odorant receptors (ORs) are ligand-gated ion channels, yet how ligand binding is coupled to pore opening remains poorly understood. Here, we combine more than 400 $\mu$s of aggregate molecular dynamics simulations and adaptive sampling with Markov state models (MSMs) and electrophysiological measurements to characterize the gating dynamics of \textit{Aedes aegypti} odorant receptor 10 (AaegOR10). Interaction analysis identifies M288 as a persistent contact between $o$-cresol and S6, connecting the orthosteric pocket to a conformation-dependent hydrophobic network involving I293, F294, and F356 at the S6-S7b interface. The MSMs place the experimentally determined open and closed structures within a multistate conformational landscape and identify a principal intermediate along the dominant gating pathway. A localized S6 kink in this state is associated with weakened S6-S7b coupling and increased flexibility of the pore-lining S7b helix. Ligand binding shifts the conformational equilibrium toward open states and shortens the transition times from the closed state to both the intermediate and open states. We also identify an off-path closed state characterized by a pronounced inward displacement of S6, with phospholipid headgroup insertion observed in some sampled conformations. Mutational analysis and voltage-clamp recordings support the functional relevance of M288, the S6-S7b interface, and the kink-prone S6 region. Together, these results describe a multistate pathway linking ligand recognition to AaegOR10 pore gating.
affiliations: Zhejiang University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Spatial context of cellular heterogeneity in triple-negative breast cancer reveals actionable subtypes
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive, heterogeneous disease with limited targeted treatment options. Leveraging bulk and spatial transcriptomics and cellular mapping of breast tissue from a large patient cohort, we identified three reproducible TNBC ecosystem subtypes that encode distinct spatial tumor-microenvironment architectures and clinically relevant treatment-response phenotype. Our analyses define: (1) an immune-exhausted subtype associated with immune checkpoint therapy (ICT); (2) a highly fibrotic/hypoxic subtype; and (3) a metabolically reprogrammed subtype characterized by nuclear-receptor and fatty-acid signaling. Spatial profiling further revealed subtype-specific organization of epithelial, immune, and stromal programs across tumor centers and invasive edges. Multiplexed imaging independently supported the contrasting immune-infiltrated and stromal-excluded architectures of the immune-engaged and fibrotic subtypes. The unique markers associated with the subtypes also provide the basis for subtyping and candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities. Our study provides a robust framework for personalized medicine, highlighting that targeting specific spatio-cellular architectures is critical to improving clinical outcomes.
affiliations: UC San Diego (corresponding author)

papers.title: Common cis-eQTLs do not explain chromosome 21 expression deviations from the ploidy expectation in Down syndrome
papers.abstract: Down syndrome (DS) results from trisomy 21 (T21), the triplication of human chromosome 21 (HSA21). On average, genes on HSA21 are overexpressed at the expected 1.5-fold increase. A small subset of HSA21 genes is expressed closer to euploid levels. Could local genetic regulatory variation explain deviations from the expected dosage? Using the largest DS-specific transcriptomic dataset to date from the Human Trisome Project (HTP) and GTEx expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), we tested whether local genetic regulatory variation contributes to gene-specific buffering or amplification of HSA21 dosage effects in DS. We compared the bulk RNA-seq profiles of protein-coding genes, lncRNAs, and pseudogenes from whole-blood samples of 274 participants with T21 and 80 euploid (D21) participants. We filtered out genes with low read counts or high genomic repeat content and applied ploidy correction to the differential expression analysis. We found 13 genes that differed significantly from the expected fold change. We cross-referenced GTEx whole-blood eQTLs (cis window 1 {+/-} Mb) with the 13 deviating genes. A common cis-eQTL was detected for 8 of the 10 testable genes. However, 59 of 99 HSA21 genes that had the expected fold change had significant cis-eQTLs. Additionally, T21 participants carry the eQTL alleles at similar frequencies to GTEx donors. Therefore, cis-eQTLs explain differences between people with T21, not the difference between T21 and D21. Overall, common cis-regulatory variation acts on HSA21 genes in T21 as it does in euploid blood, but it does not explain which genes deviate from the ploidy expectation.
affiliations: University of Colorado Anschutz (corresponding author)

papers.title: A role for CIZ1, a Nuclear Matrix Protein Overexpressed in Cancer Cells, in Controlling the Initiation of DNA Replication
papers.abstract: DNA replication licensing is tightly coordinated with cell-cycle progression to ensure genome stability. Here we demonstrate that CIZ1, a nuclear matrix scaffold protein in human cells, coordinates DNA replication licensing through direct interactions with the Origin Recognition Complex (ORC), CDC6, and Cyclins E/A-CDK2. The C-terminal zinc finger region of CIZ1 mediates binding to the cyclin-binding motifs of ORC1 and CDC6, and Cyclin -CDK-dependent phosphorylation regulates these interactions. Cell cycle analyses demonstrated a dynamic association of CIZ1 with ORC1 and CDC6. Functional studies showed that CIZ1 depletion impaired MCM loading, reduced DNA synthesis, delayed S-phase progression and inhibited cell proliferation. Cancer cells overexpressing CIZ1 exhibited an enhanced dependency on its expression, and CRISPR tiling screens identified the C-terminal regulatory region containing cyclin-binding motifs and CDK phosphorylation sites as essential for cell proliferation. Acute degradation of CIZ1 further revealed an unexpected role in maintaining CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) occupancy at specific genomic loci and regulating transcriptional programs associated with cell adhesion and migration, indicating that CIZ1 links DNA replication with higher-order genome organization. Finally, depletion of CIZ1 significantly suppressed colorectal tumor growth in xenograft models. Together, these findings establish CIZ1 as a multifunctional scaffold that integrates DNA replication licensing, Cyclin -CDK signaling, and chromatin architecture.
affiliations: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (corresponding author)

papers.title: Histone H2A.X contributes to Gene Expression Regulation and Cell-Cycle Progression in Toxoplasma gondii Tachyzoites
papers.abstract: Histone H2A.X is a conserved variant classically associated with the DNA damage response (DDR), where its phosphorylation ({gamma}H2A.X) marks double-strand breaks and recruits repair factors. H2A.X is absent in many parasitic protozoans such as Plasmodium, Trypanosoma and Leishmania. In Toxoplasma gondii, the obligate intracellular parasite, causative agent of toxoplasmosis, however, its presence raises the question of whether it contributes to genome stability. To tackle this, we generated a T. gondii knockout of H2A.X (RH{Delta}H2A.X) and evaluated its phenotype. Although H2A.X is phosphorylated in response to DNA damage in T. gondii as in other systems, RH{Delta}H2A.X parasites showed no increased sensitivity to genotoxic agents, indicating that H2A.X is dispensable for canonical DDR. Instead, loss of H2A.X caused reduced gliding motility, increased host cell invasion and clustering of extracellular parasites after egress. Despite no defects in replication rate, RH{Delta}H2A.X showed delayed mitotic progression with abnormal vacuole morphology. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a moderate yet coordinated reprogramming of protein-coding genes. Specifically, H2A.X loss altered the expression of key apical secretory and virulence factors, especially ROP18, while inducing the transcriptional activation of mitotic and DNA replication machinery. Differential enrichment analysis further revealed that upregulated genes were preferentially associated with S phase, whereas downregulated genes were enriched during mitosis and cytokinesis. This is consistent with the delayed mitotic progression and spindle abnormalities observed by microscopy and flow cytometry and suggests a cell cycle phase-specific mechanism of H2A.X-dependent transcriptional control. Rather than a driver of DDR, these findings suggest that T. gondii H2A.X operates as a chromatin organizer that coordinates cell division fidelity and virulence gene expression.
affiliations: CONICET La Plata (corresponding author)

papers.title: Continuous Large Maf Activity Maintains Fast Myofiber Identity and Multicellular Homeostasis in Adult Skeletal Muscle
papers.abstract: Fast myofibers are preferentially affected during aging, exhibiting atrophy and shifts toward slower myofiber programs, yet the mechanisms preserving established fast-fiber identity remain unclear. Here, we show that the large Maf transcription factors Mafa, Mafb, and Maf are continuously required to maintain type IIb myofiber identity in adult skeletal muscle. Inducible deletion of large Mafs caused near-complete loss of type IIb fibers, a transition toward type IIx/IIa states, reduced strength, and increased fatigue resistance. RNA-seq and ATAC-seq revealed transcriptional and chromatin accessibility remodeling across the fast myosin locus, characterized by persistent loss of Myh4 expression and increased accessibility around Myh1. Single-nucleus RNA-seq identified transient myonuclei co-expressing multiple myosin isoforms before emergence of a Myh1-dominant state, accompanied by remodeling of non-myonuclear cell populations. These changes shared features with aging- and denervation-associated muscle remodeling. Thus, continuous large Maf activity maintains adult fast myofiber identity and coordinates skeletal muscle tissue homeostasis.
affiliations: University of Tsukuba (corresponding author)

papers.title: Plakoglobin supports length-dependent force generation and cardiac resistance to fasting
papers.abstract: Mechanical activity protects muscle from atrophy, but how contractile forces relate to anabolic signaling remains unclear. We previously showed that plakoglobin promotes insulin-PI3K-AKT-FoxO signaling and that its loss causes skeletal muscle atrophy. Here, super-resolution microscopy revealed that plakoglobin localizes with desmin at the sarcolemma and is lost from the membrane during fasting-induced skeletal muscle atrophy. In skinned muscle fibers, plakoglobin downregulation impaired stretch-induced increase in myofilament activation at long sarcomere length. During fasting, skeletal muscle lost sarcolemmal plakoglobin-containing complexes, insulin signaling, and mass and induced MuRF1 and MAFbx/Atrogin1. In contrast, cardiac muscle retained these complexes and anabolic signaling, and maintained its mass. Cardiac plakoglobin also resisted AAV-shJUP-mediated depletion despite viral delivery. Moreover, MEK inhibition disrupted this cardiac response, reduced AKT signaling, induced atrogenes, and decreased cardiac mass. Thus, plakoglobin supports force generation at increased sarcomere length, and preservation of plakoglobin-containing complexes and MEK-ERK signaling accompany cardiac resistance to fasting-induced atrophy.
affiliations: Technion Institute of Technology (corresponding author)

papers.title: Single-Cell Multimodal Profiling Reveals Maternal Diabetes-Nkx2-5 Interaction in Congenital Heart Disease in a Genetic Model Recapitulating Human Embryopathies
papers.abstract: The etiological complexity of congenital heart disease (CHD) arises from the interaction between genetic and environmental factors. We hypothesized that environmental exposure could potentiate a genetic susceptibility, leading to an increased incidence of specific cardiac defects. To test this hypothesis, we used betaV59M+ female mice exhibiting severe hyperglycemia (>28 mmol/L) without dyslipidemia, a model we characterized that faithfully recapitulates human diabetic embryopathy. These females were crossed with males haploinsufficient for Nkx2-5, a transcription factor essential for cardiac development and implicated in human CHD. Our results show that the combination of genetic susceptibility and a hyperglycemic maternal environment (GxE) leads to a higher frequency and severity of cardiac malformations, including ventricular septal defects specifically involving the muscular septum, univentricular morphologies, and dilation with thinning of the myocardium. These structural abnormalities were associated with transcriptional changes affecting the contractile identity of the chamber myocardium. Single-nucleus multiomic profiling (snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq) of the E9.5 cardiac region revealed that the interaction between maternal diabetes and Nkx2-5 haploinsufficiency profoundly reshapes transcriptional and chromatin accessibility landscapes. These changes affect not only metabolic pathways, but also cell cycle progression in second heart field (SHF) progenitors, likely contributing to the observed structural cardiac defects. Multiomic integration further identifies a disrupted indirect Nkx2-5-Aldh1a2 regulatory axis in posterior SHF progenitors, while demonstrating that maternal diabetes selectively affects a restricted subset of Nkx2-5-dependent regulatory elements associated with cardiomyocyte maturation. Our findings establish a comprehensive single-cell multiomic resource that will facilitate the integration of human GWAS and other genomic datasets, enabling the identification and functional interpretation of disease-associated loci.
affiliations: Aix Marseille Univ, INSERM, INRAE, C2VN, Marseille, France (corresponding author)

papers.title: SorCS2 controls Wnt signaling homeostasis during neurodevelopment by regulating Ror2 activity and trafficking
papers.abstract: Wnt signaling orchestrates key developmental processes, yet mechanisms restricting its spatial and temporal activity remain incompletely understood. Here we identify SorCS2, a VPS10p-domain sorting receptor, as a conserved regulator of Wnt signaling homeostasis. Integrating proteomics, cell biology, embryology, and vertebrate models, we show that SorCS2 interacts with the noncanonical Wnt receptor Ror2 and controls its trafficking, Wnt5a-induced internalization, and lysosomal degradation. In mouse dopaminergic progenitors, SorCS2 deficiency enhances responsiveness to canonical and noncanonical Wnt ligands, increases Ror2 phosphorylation, and amplifies downstream signaling of both Wnt signaling cascades. Loss of SorCS2 further disrupts the ligand-receptor feedback loop, leading to elevated Ror2, Wnt5a, and Wnt1 expression, accelerated proliferation and neurogenesis, and increased expression of Tcf4, a gene implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders. Across vertebrate systems, SorCS2-dependent control of Ror2 signaling is required for anterior-posterior axis elongation, convergent extension, somitogenesis, and brain morphogenesis. These findings define a SorCS2-dependent sorting mechanism that fine-tunes morphogen receptor signaling during vertebrate neurodevelopment.
affiliations: Aarhus University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Thermoplastic polyurethane as a base material for soft, high-density neural interfaces
papers.abstract: Polymers used as substrate and encapsulation for implantable devices are typically deposited layer-by-layer, leaving polymer-polymer interfaces that adhere poorly and become a critical failure point. Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) elastomers combine four properties not found together in any other candidate: decades of clinical use in long-term implants and availability in medical grade, a stiffness well below that of polyimide and parylene C, compatibility with microfabrication, and thermoplastic self-fusion, which removes the polymer-polymer interface entirely. This work introduces TPU as a base material for soft, high-density neural interfaces and demonstrates one route to realizing them. Gold is patterned on a sacrificial copper sheet by maskless lithography and transferred into TPU by vacuum lamination, giving conformally coated tracks down to 15 um at 30 um pitch within a single, merged polymer body. An additional electroplating step produces a nanostructured pinecone gold surface that increases the electrochemically active area of the electrodes, approximately doubling the charge injection capacity. Daisy-chain silicon chips were also embedded within the soft polymer body. The films transmit up to 88% at 470 nm, a wavelength commonly used for optogenetics. TPU showed no cytotoxicity towards differentiated SH-SY5Y cells and only a mild tissue response after 9.5 months of subcutaneous implantation in rats.
affiliations: Department of Microelectronics, Delft University of Technology, Delft, The Netherlands (corresponding author)

papers.title: Pharmacologically targeting CDK12 induces BRCAness and synergizes with merestinib to exacerbate DNA damage in high-risk neuroblastoma
papers.abstract: Goulding et al. pharmacologically target CDK12 in neuroblastoma cells to downregulate DNA damage repair gene expression, resulting in apoptosis. The multi-kinase inhibitor merestinib emerged as highly synergistic with CDK12 inactivation, exacerbating DNA damage. Orally bioavailable CDK12/13 inhibitor, OKI-1546, impeded neuroblastoma tumor growth in vivo, with merestinib enhancing this anti-tumor effect.

papers.title: genomeRxiv: a genome-based identification web server that bridges the gap between taxonomy and strain typing
papers.abstract: Precise identification depends on highly resolved classification. Therefore, whole genome-based strain typing schemes have been implemented for identification of the most important microbial human pathogens. However, there are no dedicated typing schemes for the majority of prokaryotic human, animal, and plant pathogens, or for non-pathogenic microbes, often limiting their identification to taxonomic classification tools that have the species as the smallest unit. To address this deficiency, we created the genomeRxiv web server which contains over 350,000 genomes and leverages the average nucleotide identity (ANI)-based Life Identification Number (LIN) approach, allowing users to identify prokaryotic genomes in real time from approximately genus-rank to near strain-level resolution. LINs are overlaid with circumscriptions of species and infraspecies classes, integrating taxonomy with strain typing. Metadata and distance trees are visualized to complement inferred phylogenetic relationships with epidemiological and ecological information. A command line tool is provided for users to upload k-mer sketches of unpublished genomes and associated metadata, facilitating epidemiological investigations without the need to share complete DNA sequences. In conclusion, genomeRxiv constitutes a much-needed resource for precise, rapid identification of the many prokaryotes not included in any pathogen-specific typing scheme.
affiliations: Virginia Tech (corresponding author)

papers.title: Triacylglycerol fatty acid composition modulates ATGL regioselectivity and diacylglycerol output
papers.abstract: Adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) catalyses the first and rate-limiting step of intracellular triacylglycerol (TAG) hydrolysis, yielding diacylglycerol (DAG) and a free fatty acid (FA). The site of TAG cleavage determines the regioisomeric identity of the DAG product, with distinct consequences for downstream signalling and lipid metabolism. Here, we show that ATGL prefers specific fatty acyl chain lengths and that this preference contributes to its regioselectivity on heterogeneous TAG substrates. Structural modelling identified a substrate-binding pocket comprising a hydrophilic anchor and a hydrophobic tunnel whose dimensions favour long-chain FAs. Mass spectrometry-based analysis of DAG products generated by ATGL from defined TAG substrates revealed an intrinsic preference for terminal (sn-1/sn-3) ester bond cleavage. Acyl-chain compatibility modulated this preference, with poorly accommodated terminal chains increasing the relative contribution of sn-2 cleavage. Consequently, ATGL generated predominantly sn-2-retaining DAG species from heterogeneous TAG substrates containing long-chain fatty acyl chains, including substantial amounts of the sn-1,2-DAG regioisomer, which has not previously been associated with ATGL activity. These findings link the fatty acyl chain composition of TAGs to the DAG regioisomer profile generated by ATGL-mediated lipolysis and provide substrate-dependent parameters for more species-resolved models of lipid metabolism.
affiliations: University of Graz (corresponding author)

papers.title: Andes virus from the MV Hondius outbreak is highly pathogenic in hamsters and airborne shed
papers.abstract: In May 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) caused by Andes virus (ANDV) was detected aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, sparking public health measures in multiple countries. ANDV infections in humans are mostly sporadic, most often linked to exposure to infected rodents in South America, although small clusters of human cases, like the 2026 outbreak on the MV Hondius occur as well. It is not known whether virological factors may contribute to this distinct epidemiology, and no phenotypic characterisation of the newly emerged ANDV (ANDV2026) has been carried out to date. Here, using an ANDV isolate from a presymptomatic patient from the MV Hondius, we studied pathogenesis, identified sites of viral replication, characterized innate and adaptive immune responses, and quantified shedding in golden Syrian hamsters. ANDV2026 proved to be highly pathogenic in hamsters, causing severe pulmonary disease reminiscent of HPS. ANDV2026 triggered a delayed type-I IFN response and inflammatory response in the lungs consistent with the key pathological features of HPS, and we detected viral replication in both respiratory and extra-respiratory tissues, including the brain. Infected animals mounted neutralising antibodies and T cell responses, the latter directed predominantly against the L and N proteins. Importantly, ANDV2026-infected animals shed virus through multiple routes, and we detected infectious virus in air samplers connected to cages housing ANDV2026-infected hamsters. In contrast, control hamsters infected with a rodent-derived ANDV isolate (ANDV9717869) shed little virus and air samples were consistently negative. These findings consolidate established features of ANDV pathogenesis, while revealing properties not previously described. Phenotypic characterisation of patient-derived ANDV isolates in animal models can strengthen outbreak preparedness, identify markers of disease severity, and support the development of medical countermeasures.
affiliations: Department of Viroscience, Erasmus University Medical Center, Rotterdam, the Netherlands (corresponding author)

Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
papers.abstract: Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

papers.title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
papers.abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

papers.title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
papers.abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
papers.abstract: Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls ( Tyto alba ) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

papers.title: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination
papers.abstract: Genome stability is essential for cellular viability yet constantly threatened by DNA-damaging agents. Among these, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are particularly harmful and in S/G2 phases are faithfully repaired through homologous recombination (HR). The RAD51 recombinase forms nucleoprotein filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that performs critical functions in HR. The efficiency of HR depends on precise regulation of RAD51 filament dynamics by accessory factors, including RAD54B, a double-strand DNA-dependent ATPase. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays, we show that RAD54B stabilizes RAD51–DNA filaments, inhibits RAD51 ATPase activity, and promotes D-loop formation and strand exchange. RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β-domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B’s ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells. Our findings uncover a modular architecture and mechanistic framework for RAD54B’s critical role in genome maintenance.

Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
papers.abstract: Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.

papers.title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
papers.abstract: Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

papers.title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
papers.abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

papers.title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
papers.abstract: Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

papers.title: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants
papers.abstract: Single-molecule techniques provide exceptional resolution of biomolecular dynamics but are limited by low throughput. Here, we present a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel kinetic profiling of multiple protein variants in a single experiment. Each protein is covalently linked to a unique DNA barcode, decoded through transient hybridisation of fluorescent probes distinguished by colour and binding duration. Applied to a library of 16 ClpS variants, this approach revealed ~5-fold variation in dissociation kinetics and uncovered previously unrecognised bimodal binding behaviour arising from distinct structural subpopulations. By enabling scalable, multiplexed functional characterisation at the single-molecule level, this platform provides a general framework for protein engineering, directed evolution and the development of next-generation single-molecule technologies.
