Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

papers.title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
papers.abstract: The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c + ), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c + . Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Anomalous spin–lattice coupling in a 2D antiferromagnetic semiconductor revealed by surface acoustic Rayleigh waves
papers.abstract: Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS 3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

papers.title: Ultrahigh-speed chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry
papers.abstract: Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Despite these advancements, the imaging capability of time-resolved SS-FPP is still limited by the flexibility and speed of both pattern projection and image acquisition, as well as by the duration of the observation time window. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara’s fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. These results highlight C-BLIP’s promise for continuous-streaming, ultrahigh-speed 3D metrology in industrial inspection, bionics, and data security.

papers.title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
papers.abstract: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNA Ile complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
papers.abstract: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

papers.abstract: By using a novel computational framework, a cross-sectional analysis on laboratory data from two independent cohorts reveals that the final menstrual period marks an abrupt, multisystem physiological shift, with sex hormone changes beginning more than 10 years before menopause onset.

papers.title: Early-career balancing act: training, moving, relationships and language learning
papers.abstract: These early career scientists in Europe share challenges and advice about finding the ‘right’ lab and lab–life blend.

papers.title: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival
papers.abstract: Single-micronucleus sequencing and live-cell imaging of cancer cells, as well as analyses of biopsies from patients with neuroblastoma, reveal that ecDNA in micronuclei limits tumor cell fitness and is associated with patient survival.

papers.title: Author Correction: p300 nucleocytoplasmic shuttling underlies mTORC1 hyperactivation in Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome
Author Correction: A first-in-class selective inhibitor of EGFR and PI3K offers a single-molecule approach to targeting adaptive resistance
Author Correction: Biomimetic graphitic carbon nitride nanoparticles for multiscale photomodulation and therapeutic intervention
EpCAM-dependent membrane mechanics regulate nuclear deformation and promote gastric cancer metastasis
papers.abstract: Chen et al. identify EpCAM as a regulator of membrane-cytoskeletal mechanics in diffuse gastric cancer. EpCAM-associated ERM-actin remodeling couples altered membrane mechanics with nuclear deformation and confined migration, providing a mechanical framework for understanding EpCAM-associated gastric cancer progression.

papers.title: Subpopulation networks: a scaling principle for engineering living systems
papers.abstract: Cell populations underpin applications ranging from bioproduction and biotherapeutics to microbiome engineering and biocomputing. However, treating them as bulk quantities rather than as structured systems limits our understanding of population-level stability, productivity, and robustness. Cellular populations self-organize into coexisting subpopulations (SPs) representing phenotypically distinct states that emerge from the interplay of biological noise and selective pressures. We propose that networks of interacting SPs constitute a fundamental organizational layer for engineering stable cell population dynamics. Surveying published single-cell studies across bacterial, yeast, and mammalian systems, we show that populations consistently self-organize into a limited number of SPs. This dimensional reduction can be captured experimentally by clustering single-cell data and gives rise to scaling laws that link population structure to collective performance.

papers.title: Characterisation of Genetically-Derived Patient Clusters Highlights Genetic Heterogeneity of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
papers.abstract: Background and aims. Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) is a complex immune-mediated condition with a strong genetic contribution. The genetics of IBD are highly complex, with inflammation, autoimmunity, and mucosal immunity pathways involved in its pathogenicity. GenePy is a gene-level disease burden metric. The integration of clinical and genetic data and the application of machine learning methods can aid patient stratification for personalised care. Methods. Lists of consensus IBD pathway genes were curated. GenePy scores were computed from whole exome sequencing data. A K-Means algorithm was optimised using clustering quality and stability metrics on the GenePy scores of genes in each IBD pathway, and the results replicated in three independent IBD cohorts (SPARC IBD, MSCCR IBD, and Southampton IBD). Chi-square tests assessed the association between cluster assignment and phenotypic features, and were multiple test corrected via Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Results. A strong association was replicated for NOD signalling genes driving IBD subtype, Crohns disease behaviour, and IBD surgery across all cohorts, as well as granuloma in Southampton IBD. This was mainly driven by NOD2. Similar genetic clustering patterns were observed across all cohorts, with additional phenotypic enrichment in clusters driven by NLRP1 (surgery in MSCCR IBD), and nominally significant enrichment for disease behaviour linked to BIRC2 (B2 in Southampton IBD and B2B3 in SPARC IBD). Conclusions. This analysis identified a common genetic architecture across NOD signalling genes across IBD cohorts, replicated a signal for NOD2 as a monogenic driver of disease with a strong phenotypic enrichment, and identified other putative genetic drivers of IBD, such as the NLRP1 gene.
affiliations: Human Genetics and Genomic Medicine, University of Southampton, Southampton, UK (corresponding author)

papers.title: ABC transporters support Drosophila intestinal stem and progenitor cells during cytotoxic challenge
papers.abstract: Adult stem cells can survive diverse insults, from ionizing radiation to toxic chemicals. In vertebrates, ABC transporter expression and dye-efflux capacity have been associated with stem-cell protection and multidrug resistance. How compound accumulation differs between adult stem cells and their differentiated daughters within an intact tissue remains poorly understood. Here, we show that adult Drosophila intestinal stem/progenitor cells maintain a distinct low-accumulation state for membrane-permeable compounds and that ABC transporters contribute to this phenotype and to the response to cytotoxic stress. Across nine membrane-permeable probes, stem/progenitor cells accumulated eight at lower levels than differentiated enterocytes. We selected tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester (TMRM), a membrane-permeable fluorescent probe that showed a strong difference in accumulation between stem/progenitor cells and enterocytes, as a quantitative readout for an RNAi screen of all 56 Drosophila ABC-family genes. The screen identified seven candidate transporters whose depletion increased the stem/progenitor-to-enterocyte TMRM fluorescence ratio. Further characterization of one of them, ABCB7, showed that ABCB7-depleted guts contained fewer mitotic cells during cytotoxic drug exposure. These results implicate ABC transporters in lower compound accumulation in Drosophila intestinal stem/progenitor cells and support a role for ABC transporters in their response to cytotoxic challenge.
affiliations: Harvard Medical School (corresponding author)

papers.title: Probing Physical Intuition in Large Language Models through Partner-Dependent Mutation Prediction
papers.abstract: Structure-guided mutation design requires relating a proposed substitution to its molecular environment to anticipate its effects. Existing evaluations of large language models (LLMs) in protein engineering emphasize sequence-based prediction or tool-integrated workflows, leaving unclear whether LLMs themselves can infer mutation effects from structural evidence without dedicated predictors. We evaluate physical intuition-qualitative reasoning that connects structural observations with molecular interaction principles-using a benchmark that tests the same substitution in the same protein across different binding partners, with predictions based on local atomic coordinates and no dedicated mutation-effect predictors. In the tested comparisons, the best-performing LLM achieved group accuracy comparable to the evaluated energy predictors and Biomni, an LLM-driven tool workflow, while the methods differed in their prediction patterns. Most evaluated LLMs achieved higher group accuracy for larger affinity improvements. Structural interventions support selective dependence on mutation-site and partner information, while assessable structural claims largely agree with the supplied coordinates. These findings support direct LLM structural reasoning as a basis for developing rational mutation-design tools that connect molecular observations with partner-specific effects.
affiliations: Department of Bioinformatics and Biostatistics, School of Life Sciences and Biotechnology, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (corresponding author)

papers.title: tRNAZAP: Deep learning toolkit for nanopore tRNA signal analysis
papers.abstract: tRNA are short, ~76 nucleotide-long, modification-rich molecules that play an important role in protein translation. Nanopore sequencing is the only platform capable of directly sequencing full-length, native tRNA molecules. This capability is enabled by splinted ligation of tRNA-specific adapters. As a result, the measured ionic current signal reflects a composition of both adapter and tRNA sequence features. Despite these advantages, analysis of nanopore tRNA sequencing data poses distinct computational challenges. Existing ionic current-based signal-to-sequence decoding (basecalling) models are optimized for mRNA and perform suboptimally on short, modification-dense RNA such as tRNA. Furthermore, alignment algorithms for reference-guided analysis of short-length reads are not optimized for nanopore reads with lower accuracy than Next-generation sequencing reads. To overcome these limitations, domain-specific computational approaches are required. We present tRNAZAP, a nanopore ionic current signal analysis toolkit designed to enable precise reference-guided sequence alignment. tRNAZAP operates directly on raw ionic current signals and decomposes the analysis into two complementary tasks: 1) segmentation of adapter and tRNA regions, and 2) tRNA classification, both implemented using transformer-based models. The segmentation component isolates the tRNA signal portion and extracts the corresponding nucleotide sequence as the alignment query, while the classification component identifies the tRNA type as the alignment reference without requiring sequence-level information. Together, these outputs allow direct optimal pairwise alignment between the tRNA subsequence of the full query and reference sequences. Trained on in vitro transcribed RNA data and evaluated on yeast tRNA, these models achieved ~98% classification accuracy and intersection-over-union of ~0.98 for segmentation.
affiliations: Northeastern University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Region-Specific Host Responses in Amoebic Gill Disease of Atlantic Salmon
papers.abstract: Amoebic gill disease (AGD), caused by the parasite Neoparamoeba perurans, is a major welfare and economic burden for the Atlantic salmon aquaculture industry. However, the spatial organisation of immune functions within the gill, the site of infection, remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the first spatial transcriptomic atlas of the Atlantic salmon gill affected by AGD, generated using 10x Genomics Visium on four AGD-positive fish, confirmed by gill scoring and quantitative PCR for parasite load. As no uninfected gills were included, this study maps the anatomical and immunological organisation of AGD-affected gills rather than defining AGD-specific pathology. Unsupervised clustering of spatial gene expression resolved distinct transcriptional domains that grouped into four principal anatomical compartments of the gill, including (i) epithelial and lamellar regions defined by keratin and osmoregulatory gene expression, (ii) gill arch regions enriched for connective tissue and smooth muscle markers, (iii) an erythroid-associated vascular cluster, and (iv) a skeletal muscle cluster with signatures of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation. Across these domains, we identified a spatially organised and diffused immune landscape, with pattern recognition receptors, antimicrobial effectors and chemokines concentrated at the filament surface, and immunoglobulin light chain transcripts consistent with B lymphocyte activity enriched toward the gill arch. Integration of the spatial data with a published single-nucleus reference atlas using reference-based deconvolution resolved the cellular identity underlying these domains and revealed frequent co-localisation of immune and structural cell types, suggesting regulated cell to cell communication within the gill-associated lymphoid tissue. Overall, our results show that the Atlantic salmon gill is not a transcriptionally uniform surface but a regionally specialised organ, with immune functions distributed across, and specialised within, distinct anatomical compartments
affiliations: University of Glasgow (corresponding author)

papers.title: Maintenance of restriction-modification system diversity creates pan-immunity
papers.abstract: Bacterial antiviral defense systems are highly diverse and unevenly distributed across populations, such that different strains carry distinct immune repertoires that together form a pan-immune system. Restriction-modification (RM) systems are the most abundant bacterial defense systems and exemplify this architecture, exhibiting remarkable diversity in structure, function, specificity, and efficacy. How and why such diversity is maintained, why weaker systems are not outcompeted, and whether diversity provides benefits beyond protection of individual cells remain unclear. Here, we experimentally tracked bacteria and phages across populations differing in RM diversity. We find no consistent evidence of a trade-off between defense strength and host fitness. Instead, we identify a trade-off between defense strength and horizontal transferability: stronger RM systems are less able to spread between strains, likely because factors that increase defense strength also increase toxicity risk upon transfer to unmethylated hosts. These weaker yet more mobile systems may therefore act as more accessible pan-immune components that bacterial populations can acquire in response to shifting parasite pressures. Furthermore, we show RM systems experience negative frequency-dependent selection, such that common specificities are more readily overcome by phages while rare ones remain protective, causing the benefits of potent systems to erode as they spread. Together, these dynamics maintain RM diversity and explain why weaker systems persist alongside stronger ones. Finally, we show that population-level RM diversity generates collective protection by constraining the emergence of RM-escaping phages and limiting the invasion of bacterial surface mutants that avoid phage adsorption, providing experimental support for the pan-immune model.
affiliations: University of Exeter (corresponding author)

papers.title: Metabolic reorganization shapes the dynamics of a water kefir microbial community
papers.abstract: Microbial fermentations emerge from the collective activity of interacting species whose relative abundances, metabolic functions, and environmental constraints continuously change over time. Water kefir provides a tractable model to investigate how multispecies communities coordinate their metabolic activities during fermentation. Here, we combined time-resolved community profiling, physicochemical measurements, metabolite quantification, and controlled co-culture assays to characterize the dynamics of a water kefir consortium comprising 19 detected microbial species. Our results reveal that water kefir fermentation is not adequately described as a simple succession of independently acting microbial groups. Instead, the community undergoes a reproducible reorganization of its collective metabolism around 20 h of fermentation. This transition marks a shift from an early regime characterized by the accumulation of soluble sugars and ethanol to a later regime dominated by enhanced sugar consumption and lactate production. Controlled interaction assays further showed that bacterial partners can alter carbon-use behaviour in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, highlighting the capacity of interspecies interactions to reshape metabolic phenotypes within the consortium. Together, these results support an ecological view of water kefir fermentation in which community-wide metabolic reorganization emerges from the interplay between microbial interactions, resource availability, and environmental change.
affiliations: Museum National d'Histoire Naturelle (corresponding author)

papers.title: Genome-wide CRISPRi mapping of mycobacteriophage interaction determinants in Mycobacterium smegmatis mc2155
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages are highly specific predators of bacterial hosts, but the molecular mechanisms governing their entry across the structurally complex mycobacterial cell envelope remain poorly defined. Utilizing a genome-wide CRISPR interference library in the model organism Mycobacterium smegmatis against a phylogenetically representative collection of 70 mycobacteriophages, we mapped the functional architecture of host susceptibility determinants. This parallelized genetic screen revealed a spatial continuum of infection requirements spanning from outer leaflet surface structures down to deep cytoplasmic machinery. The four major outer membrane Mycobacterium smegmatis porins (Msp) emerged as the dominant candidate receptor family for 46 diverse phages, representing the first protein receptors identified within this group. Interrogating the asymmetric outer bilayer also implicated cell envelope glycolipids as candidate receptors for 14 phages, resolving into glycopeptidolipid sub-lineages. Beneath the mycomembrane, arabinogalactan functions as a candidate secondary receptor for 5 phages, while the inner membrane lipid transporter MmpL11 and the global nucleoid-associated protein Lsr2 represent determinant factors for 14 and 31 phages respectively. While physical deletions of major porins trigger spontaneous regulatory pathways that upregulate silent backup paralogues, acute transcriptional knockdowns circumvent suppressor accumulation, revealing unmasked single-gene dependencies. Structural analysis demonstrated that host determinant usage decouples entirely from whole-genome viral phylogeny, indicating that standard phylogenetic groupings fail to predict surface recognition profiles. Ultimately, mapping this host interactome reveals an evolutionary strategy where phages target highly redundant or abundant host machinery to exploit fixed physiological liabilities, presenting a robust molecular blueprint for the rational engineering of escape-resistant therapeutic phage cocktails.
affiliations: Environmental Genomics and Systems Biology Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, California, USA; Biological Systems and Engineering, Lawre (corresponding author)

papers.title: An Analog-Sensitive Tau Tubulin Kinase 2 Enables Acute Chemical-Genetic Control of Primary Cilia
papers.abstract: Kinases regulate a broad spectrum of cellular processes, including the formation of primary cilia, microtubule-based organelles that protrude from the cell surface and play important roles in development and disease. TTBK2 is a key ciliary kinase that controls primary cilium assembly and maintenance. However, highly selective small-molecule inhibitors of TTBK2 are still lacking, representing a major bottleneck for investigating the temporal requirements and dynamics of TTBK2-dependent processes in cilia. Here, we report the first analog-sensitive variant of TTBK2, enabling rapid, reversible, and highly specific control of TTBK2 kinase activity in ciliogenesis-relevant hTERT-RPE1 cells. Using this system, we define the kinetics of CEP164 phosphorylation, cilium shortening and reassembly, and IFT88 retention at the ciliary base following acute TTBK2 inhibition and subsequent inhibitor washout. Together, our findings provide new insight into TTBK2-dependent pathways and establish analog-sensitive TTBK2 as a powerful tool for investigating the dynamics of TTBK2-regulated processes with high temporal resolution.
affiliations: Masaryk University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Spindle size scaling secures mitotic fidelity against whole-genome doubling-associated mechanical stress
papers.abstract: Although whole-genome doubling (WGD) accompanies a drastic increase in chromosome number, post-WGD cells often continue to divide. How mitosis is sustained under increased chromosome number remains largely unknown. Here, we found that WGD cells require longer mitotic spindles than isogenic diploids to maintain spindle bipolarity. WGD increased mechanical stress on spindle poles during metaphase, associated with a higher risk of pole fragmentation. Disrupting kinetochore-microtubule attachment alleviated pole stress and fragmentation in WGD cells, suggesting that WGD-linked mechanical stress arises from spindle-chromosome interactions. Artificial spindle elongation reduced the pole stress and mitigated pole fragmentation defects in WGD cells. Our findings identify chromosome gain as a critical mechanical challenge to spindle organization and establish spindle size scaling as an adaptive mechanism that preserves mitotic fidelity after WGD.
affiliations: Faculty of Advanced Life Science, Hokkaido University (corresponding author)

papers.title: A chemigenetic fluorescence lifetime-based biosensor for imaging of ERK activity
papers.abstract: Extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) governs many cellular processes, and its spatiotemporal activity dynamics are important for downstream signaling specificity. Existing fluorescent ERK activity biosensors, however, fall short in enabling spectrally multiplexed, spatially resolved, or deep tissue measurements. Here, we introduce a chemigenetic, single-fluorophore biosensor, WHaloEKAR, that reports ERK activities through changes in fluorescence lifetime. WHaloEKAR combines large lifetime changes (-0.81 ns) with the spectral versatility of the self-labeling protein HaloTag giving access to orange, red, and far-red ERK biosensors. The latter enabled the investigation of heterogeneous ERK activity at distinct subcellular locations in cultured cell lines and primary cortical rat neurons via fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM). Moreover, multiplexed FLIM measurements allowed to study ERK activity in parallel to the second messengers calcium and cyclic adenosine monophosphate. Finally, WHaloEKAR enabled the investigation of ERK activity in 3D samples as well as in live animals.
affiliations: ETH Zurich (corresponding author)

papers.title: Chloride availability limits Slc4a9-dependent salivary secretion
papers.abstract: Anion exchanger 4 (Ae4), encoded by solute carrier family 4 member 9 (Slc4a9), is required for normal salivary secretion, but how it supports fluid secretion remains poorly understood. Nearly a decade ago, we developed a mathematical model that attributed reduced secretion following Ae4 knockout primarily to Ae4 mediated monovalent cation transport. Here, we reassess that interpretation by developing a dynamic model of salivary fluid secretion informed by subsequent experimental findings. The model incorporates {beta}-adrenergic regulation of Ae4 and an additional apical chloride conductance shared by the control and knockout. To isolate the contribution of Ae4, the NKCC1 and Ae2 cycle rates calculated from the evolving control state are also prescribed in the knockout. Under these conditions, the knockout model secretes 20% less fluid over 600 seconds despite identical apical chloride conductances. The control begins with a larger intracellular chloride store and continues to acquire chloride through Ae4 during stimulation. The intracellular chloride difference increases during stimulation, whilst the weaker apical electrochemical driving force in the knockout reduces chloride export and fluid secretion. The analysis also identifies the alkalinity requirement of sustained Ae4 transport and quantifies the additional NKCC1 and Ae2 transport needed to compensate for its loss. These results support intracellular chloride availability as a mechanism linking Ae4 loss to reduced salivary secretion.
affiliations: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Xrp1 integrates cellular stress through different control modes in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Cells and tissues have the ability to respond to different stresses and maintain their homeostasis. The b-Zip transcription factor Xrp1 was found to play a pivotal role in this context in Drosophila. Xrp1 is required for the response to irradiation, in genetic conditions of ribosomal protein (Rp) deficiency leading to cell competition, and more generally in mediating the Integrated Stress Response (ISR). However, how these diverse stresses converge to and activate Xrp1 is still unclear. Our results demonstrate the existence of three separate mechanisms of Xrp1 induction. In response to Rp stress, a short isoform of Xrp1 is produced and requires the function of the ribosomal protein RpS12. In response to irradiation, a specific mRNA isoform is transcriptionally induced, which encodes the Xrp1-short protein isoform, in a p53-dependent manner. In response to the ISR, the long isoform of Xrp1 is translated by the derepression of a uORF present on the Xrp1 5'UTR, a mechanism that requires eIF2 phosphorylation, RpS12, and a transcriptional induction by ATF4. Therefore, our work provides a comprehensive understanding of the role of Xrp1 in different situations of cellular stress, illustrating the complex level of integration of the mechanisms controlling this central gene.
affiliations: CRBM, Univ Montpellier, CNRS (corresponding author)

papers.title: Intrinsically disordered regions influence protein motif usage in Drosophila Ubx and AbdA Hox proteins
papers.abstract: Hox proteins are evolutionary conserved transcription factors guiding morphogenesis in all bilaterian animals. Conservation mainly concerns the homeodomain (HD), a helix-turn-helix DNA binding motif and flanking sequences close by. Besides, sequences are poorly conserved and disordered. Here we investigate how poorly conserved Intrinsically Disordered Regions (IDRs) influence Hox protein activity, focusing on a closely related Drosophila Hox pair and using a wide range of in vivo function. Studying Drosophila Ultrabithorax (Ubx) and AbdominalA (AbdA) proteins, we find that conserved protein motifs close to the HD are differently used in Ubx and AbdA. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations identify a large set of intra-molecular interactions, notably involving poorly conserved disordered regions upstream and downstream the HD. Swapping these regions in Ubx and AbdA alters protein functions and switches motif dependency in some biological situations. This suggests that IDRs, predicted to mediate large and dynamic sets of intramolecular interactions, influence protein motif usage in a context dependent manner.
affiliations: Aix-Marseille Univ, CNRS, Developmental Biology Institute of Marseille (IBDM), IBDM-UMR 7288, Case 907, Parc Scientifique de Luminy, Marseille Cedex 09 13288, F (corresponding author)

papers.title: KDM6A Haploinsufficiency Is Insufficient to Disrupt Cochlear Structure and Auditory Function in Mouse Models of Kabuki Syndrome Type 2
papers.abstract: Objective: Kabuki syndrome type 2 (KS2) is a rare X-linked disorder caused by pathogenic variants in KDM6A and is frequently associated with hearing impairment. Because auditory phenotypes include sensorineural, conductive, and mixed hearing loss, we examined whether Kdm6a deficiency directly impairs cochlear morphology or auditory function in mice. Methods: We generated Nestin-Cre; Kdm6a conditional mutants and a germline-derived global Kdm6a deletion model using Sox2-Cre-mediated germline recombination. Auditory function and cochlear morphology were assessed by auditory brainstem responses (ABRs), distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs), and histological analyses. Results: Whole-body hemizygous or homozygous Kdm6a deletion resulted in embryonic lethality. Analyses therefore focused on Nestin-Cre; Kdm6aflox/Y males and females carrying a germline-derived heterozygous Kdm6a deletion. In Nestin-Cre mutants, ABR thresholds, wave I amplitudes and latencies, and DPOAE measures at 8, 16, and 32 kHz were comparable with littermate controls at 4 and 8 weeks. In heterozygous deletion females, ABR thresholds, wave I amplitudes and latencies at 4-64 kHz and DPOAE measures at 8, 16, and 32 kHz were comparable with male and female wild-type controls. No overt cochlear pathology was observed in either model. Conclusion: Kdm6a deficiency in the viable mouse models examined did not produce overt cochlear pathology or baseline auditory dysfunction. These findings suggest that partial Kdm6a loss alone is insufficient to produce a robust primary cochlear phenotype in young mice and highlight the potential contributions of non-cochlear, developmental, central, and later-onset mechanisms to hearing impairment in KS2. Clinically, these findings support careful evaluation for potentially treatable middle-ear disease.
affiliations: University of Florida (corresponding author)

papers.title: A comprehensive genetic study of the vaginal microbiota composition of Holstein cows
papers.abstract: The vaginal microbiota is a potentially important component of the bovine reproductive tract and has been associated with fertility, health, and production-related traits in cattle. However, the impact of host genetics on the bovine vaginal microbiota and its genetic correlations with animal performance remain largely unexplored. To investigate this, we performed a comprehensive genetic study of the vaginal microbiota in Holstein cows. Vaginal swabs from 681 lactating cows across 18 herds in Northern France were collected, along with records of fertility, milk production, and health traits. The microbiota samples were sequenced for the 16S rRNA gene, generating count tables of amplicon sequence variants (ASV). We estimated genetic parameters for vaginal microbiota -diversity (Chao1, Shannon, and Simpson indices) and {beta}-diversity (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrix), as well as the centered log-ratio (CLR)-transformed abundances of taxa present in more than 50% of samples. Across the 173 analyzed taxa, heritability estimates ranged from low to moderate (h2 = 0.09 to 0.38) for five genera, three families, eight orders, three classes, and one phylum. Notably, the order Flavobacteriales exhibited the highest heritability estimate. The study also highlighted genetic correlations between heritable microbiota traits and host phenotypes related to fertility, production, and health. Sequence-based genome-wide association studies (GWAS) identified biologically relevant signals, including a quantitative trait locus (QTL) for the genus Alloprevotella on chromosome 6, with lead variants located within the NAF1 gene. Additionally, two signals on chromosome 17 for the Bacteroidales order and the Bacteroida class co-localized with IL15. Our findings show that host genetics contributes to variation in specific components of the bovine vaginal microbiota and suggest that microbiome-related traits may warrant further investigation as potential indicators in dairy cattle breeding and management research.
affiliations: Université Paris-Saclay, INRAE, AgroParisTech, GABI, Jouy-en-Josas, 78350, France (corresponding author)

papers.title: From variants to networks: resolving low SNP overlap in dairy cattle meta-analysis through multi-level functional mapping
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to perform a systematic review and multi-level meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for functional traits in dairy cattle, focusing on calving performance and udder health. We hypothesized that despite the limited replication of individual SNPs across independent studies, functionally related variants would converge on common genes, biological pathways, and genomic regions. Following a systematic literature search and a two-stage filtering process, we extracted data from 20 independent articles covering seven traits: direct and maternal calving ease, direct and maternal stillbirth, clinical mastitis, somatic cell count, and somatic cell score. We first conducted a conventional SNP-level meta-analysis, which demonstrated minimal variant overlap across studies, preventing the detection of significant pooled effects. To resolve this low overlap, we mapped the associated variants to higher organizational levels, including genes, proteins, KEGG and Reactome pathways, and quantitative trait loci (QTL), and combined the statistical evidence using Fishers method. This multi-level functional mapping revealed significant biological convergence. At the gene level, we identified shared genes such as CCDC170 linking maternal calving ease and maternal stillbirth, while DCK, TMPRSS11F, and SLC4A4 were significant for udder health traits. Pathway-level meta-analysis highlighted major functional networks, demonstrating that mastitis-related traits were strongly associated with immune response, signal transduction, and cellular stress pathways, whereas maternal calving traits were dominated by endocrine and calcium signaling. Furthermore, our cross-trait overlap analysis identified 35 shared pathways and 30 shared QTL, reflecting a common biological architecture connecting calving difficulties and mastitis susceptibility. Notably, the innate immune system and signal transduction pathways consistently overlapped across multiple functional traits. In conclusion, conventional SNP-level meta-analysis has limited utility for integrating dairy cattle GWAS due to insufficient cross-study marker overlap. Moving from individual variants toward higher-order functional units effectively reveals reproducible genetic signals and functional convergence. The identified genes, biological pathways, and genomic regions offer valuable insights that can be leveraged as biological priors to improve genomic prediction models for dairy cattle health and reproduction.
affiliations: Wroclaw University of Enviromental and Life Sciences (corresponding author)

papers.title: ALS-associated mutations reveal a conserved C-terminal self-assembly module in the TDP-43 low-complexity domain
papers.abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is an RNA-binding protein whose low-complexity domain (LCD) mediates self-assembly, liquid-liquid phase separation, and pathological aggregation associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Previous studies have established the central ultraconserved region (UCR) of the LCD as a major determinant of TDP-43 self-association. However, the contribution of the evolutionarily conserved C-terminal region remains poorly understood. To identify LCD residues required for self-assembly, we systematically analyzed 47 ALS-associated substitutions distributed throughout the TDP-43 LCD using hydrogel-binding and thioflavin T (ThT) assays. Several ALS-associated substitutions within the C-terminal conserved region (CCR) markedly reduced hydrogel incorporation and impaired fibrillization. Similar assembly defects were observed for methionine-to-serine substitutions at two conserved CCR residues, M405 and M414. Furthermore, CCR-containing C-terminal fragments encompassing residues 360-414 or 379-414 formed ThT-positive fibrillar assemblies in vitro. The assembly kinetics exhibited a characteristic lag phase followed by rapid fluorescence growth, consistent with the formation of cross-{beta}-rich assemblies. These findings identify the CCR as an additional conserved self-assembly module within the TDP-43 LCD and expand the prevailing UCR-centered model of TDP-43 assembly. The observation that multiple ALS-associated substitutions reduce rather than enhance self-association further raises the possibility that disruption of normal TDP-43 assembly contributes to disease pathogenesis.
affiliations: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (corresponding author)

papers.title: Strategies for Overcoming the Purification Challenges of Meis1 and HoxA9 and Their Functional Characterization
papers.abstract: Transcription factors are critical regulators of homeostasis, and disruption of their function is a common underlying mechanism in cancer. The homeobox Myeloid ecotropic integration site-1 (Meis1) and its binding partner Homeobox A9 (HoxA9) are among the most highly dysregulated transcription factors in cancer, particularly in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). Upregulation of HoxA9 is observed in more than 50% of AML cases and is a predictor of poor prognosis. Meis1 forms a cooperative DNA complex with HoxA9 and is required for HoxA9-mediated leukemogenesis. However, the mechanism by which HoxA9 and Meis1 interact and form a complex with DNA is unknown. To study the molecular mechanisms behind the HoxA9-Meis1-DNA complex and support future development of inhibitors, we describe optimized procedures for the recombinant expression and purification of full-length Meis1 and HoxA9. The constructs with an N-terminal His-tag showed degradation, but the addition of a small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO)-fusion tag improved solubility and stability for both proteins. Conditions were optimized for SUMO cleavage to obtain tag-free Meis1 and HoxA9 with high purity. We showed that both purified proteins bound to DNA with nanomolar affinities using a fluorescence polarization (FP) binding assay. The SUMO-fusion HoxA9 showed a distinct binding profile compared to the tag-free HoxA9 and formed a cooperative complex with Meis1. The tag-free HoxA9 appeared to oligomerize under the assay conditions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report to visualize the HoxA9-Meis1 cooperative interaction in a high-throughput assay. Our work establishes a foundation for future studies to decipher the protein-protein interaction of Meis1-HoxA9 and the development of inhibitors.
affiliations: West Virginia University (corresponding author)

papers.title: The role of a G-quadruplex structure in mediating the interactions of miR-1249-3p with the 3-UTR of the HNRNPK mRNA
papers.abstract: Heterogenous nuclear riboprotein K (hnRNP K) is an important regulator of multiple signaling pathways involved in DNA repair and function whose expression has been found to be mis-regulated in many cancers and neurological diseases. The expression regulation of hnRNP K is not fully understood however it has been shown that the microRNA miR-1249-3p targets its mRNA 3-untranslated region (UTR), regulating its translation. In this study we identified a guanosine-rich sequence in the HNRNPK 3-UTR within the miR-1249-3p binding site that has the potential to form a G-quadruplex (GQ) structure. By using various biophysical methods, we show that this sequence forms a parallel GQ structure which modulates the binding of miR-1249-3p to HNRNPK 3-UTR in vitro. Additionally, using luciferase reporter assays, we determined that this GQ structure affects the hnRNP K protein expression, suggesting modulation of the binding interaction of miR-1249-3p to the 3-UTR of HNRNPK. This HNRNPK mRNA GQ-miR binding axis is an unexplored mechanism of regulation, offering a novel therapeutic target for diseases caused by abnormal hnRNP K expression.
affiliations: Duquesne University (corresponding author)

papers.title: A Tandem Fluorescent Rh1::eGFP mCherry Reporter Reveals Rhodopsin 1 Trafficking and Turnover In Vivo in Drosophila Photoreceptors
papers.abstract: Rhodopsin 1 (Rh1), the major visual pigment of Drosophila photoreceptors, requires a vitamin A-derived chromophore for proper folding, maturation and transport to the rhabdomere. While the endocytic trafficking of mature, light-activated Rh1 to endolysosomal compartments is well characterized, the fate of immature Rh1 during defective ER maturation remains unclear. Here, we developed a Rh1::eGFP-mCherry tandem reporter to monitor Rh1 localization and compartment acidification in vivo. Exploiting the acid stability of mCherry, this reporter enables visualization of Rh1 after delivery to acidic environments and complements conventional antibody-based approaches. Under physiological conditions, pH-dependent quenching of eGFP fluorescence distinguished rhabdomeric Rh1 from Rh1 in acidic endolysosomal compartments. In vitamin A-deficient flies, immature apo-Rh1 accumulated within Calnexin-positive ER membranes, where we identified discrete acidified subdomains characterized by loss of eGFP fluorescence while mCherry fluorescence persisted. These structures remained continuous with the ER but were distinct from conventional endolysosomal compartments, revealing previously unrecognized acidified ER domains associated with immature Rh1. Together, our findings identify acidified ER subdomains as a previously unrecognized stage in Rh1 quality control and establish Rh1::eGFP-mCherry as a robust in vivo reporter for investigating rhodopsin trafficking, maturation and turnover under physiological and disease-relevant conditions.
affiliations: Uni Hohenheim (corresponding author)

papers.title: Inter-unit variability and rapid depletion of 2,3-diphosphoglycerate in stored red blood cells: implications for transfusion practice in neurocritical care
papers.abstract: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion aims to restore tissue oxygen delivery, yet a stored unit's capacity to unload oxygen depends on 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG), the principal allosteric modulator of hemoglobin-oxygen affinity. Randomized trials comparing fresher with older units have been consistently null, and all have used storage duration as the exposure variable. We asked whether storage age reflects the metabolic state of individual units. Twenty-four leukodepleted packed RBC units were sampled serially from day 3 to day 42 of standard cold storage. 2,3-DPG was quanti-fied by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with isotopically labelled internal standards, pH was measured in parallel, and trajectories were modelled by linear mixed effects with unit-level random intercepts. At day 3, 2,3-DPG spanned a twenty-fold range across units of identical age (0.8-14.7 mol/g Hb; median 4.8): some were already near-depleted at the earliest sampled timepoint, while others retained near-physiological concentrations. This heterogeneity collapsed rapidly - median val-ues fell to 27% of day-3 levels by day 7 and by more than 90% by day 14 ({beta} = -0.298 mol/g Hb per day, p < 0.001) - and were below the limit of detection in most units af-ter day 17. pH declined monotonically to 6.40 {+/-} 0.04 by day 42 ({beta} = -0.0163 units per day, p < 0.001). Units of identical storage age therefore differ markedly in the metabo-lite that governs oxygen unloading, and virtually all are depleted long before the 42-day expiry, indicating that storage-age dichotomies misclassify the exposure they are intended to represent.

papers.title: FLEX-DBS: a flexible wireless platform for bilateral constant-current deep brain stimulation in freely moving rodents
papers.abstract: Background: Preclinical deep brain stimulation (DBS) in rodents is central to understanding how DBS works, but most rodent DBS is delivered through a tether, which constrains behavior, home-cage experiments and uninterrupted stimulation. Most long-runtime wireless mouse stimulators achieve their runtimes by setting stimulation parameters before or around implantation and operating from supplies of about 3 V. New method: FLEX-DBS (Flexible Deep Brain Stimulation) is a head-mounted, battery-powered stimulator that delivers bilateral constant-current stimulation from improved Howland current pumps on +/-5 V rails. Amplitude, pulse width and frequency are programmable in continuous and burst modes from an iOS application over Bluetooth Low Energy, and stimulation continues autonomously after the phone disconnects. The device measures 19.5 x 22.5 x 8.72 mm, weighs 3.71 g in operation and runs on two size-13 zinc-air cells, which are exchanged by briefly detaching the device, pausing stimulation only for the exchange. Results: Into a 1 k{Omega} bench load, delivered current increased approximately linearly with the amplitude setting and was repeatable from pulse to pulse, with an asymmetric biphasic waveform whose recovery phase ran at about one fifth of the stimulating amplitude. Battery current was 1.47-1.89 mA in standby and 3.15-3.42 mA during stimulation at amplitude settings of 60-400 A, giving a projected three days of continuous stimulation per pair of cells. Firmware v0.5 left a net charge of 26-35 % of the stimulating-phase charge per pulse into 1 k{Omega}. Into 47 k{Omega}, within the in vivo load range, stimulating current was compliance-limited at 93 A. Pulse-derived estimates of the effective load presented by five implanted platinum electrodes in three mice had weekly means of 43-54 k{Omega} over eight weeks (32-80 k{Omega} across individual sessions), placing the maximum regulated current near 90 A (81-101 A at the weekly means). Analysis of the current-pump network bounds load-dependent current error at 3-8% for these loads. In vivo, we delivered cingulate FLEX-DBS at high amplitude settings intended to evoke a robust stimulation-associated behavioral phenotype in six mice. Time spent immobile in an open field rose from 46.5% at baseline to 75.7% during stimulation (a 62.7% increase in the group mean) and remained elevated after stimulation ended; without a sham control, this increase cannot be separated from within-session habituation. Comparison with existing methods: Among the published wireless rodent stimulators compared here, several offer some of these capabilities, but none combines bilateral constant current output, real-time wireless control that continues as autonomous stimulation after disconnect, and both continuous and burst modes; FLEX-DBS does so at the cost of runtime measured in days rather than weeks. Conclusions: FLEX-DBS is designed for untethered DBS experiments in which parameters must be set, changed and verified at the cage. Its measured power consumption permits a projected three days of continuous operation per cell pair; firmware v0.5 requires improved charge balancing before prolonged in vivo stimulation. The electrode load, rather than the programmable range, sets the usable stimulation amplitude in vivo. In vivo, stimulation at high amplitude settings was associated with increased immobility, consistent with effective stimulation through implanted electrodes; electrode impedance and delivered current were not measured in these mice.

papers.title: Surfactant-Enhanced Hybridization Capture for Direct Sequence-Specific RNA Extraction from Plasma and Whole Blood
papers.abstract: Direct recovery of low-abundance RNA from complex biological samples remains a major challenge for ultrasensitive detection. Sequence-specific hybridization capture enables selective enrichment, but recovery from crude samples is compromised by RNA degradation, protein interference, RNA secondary structure, and target sequence variation. Here, we address these limitations with a sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)-based formulation that not only lyses virions and protects RNA, but also directly accelerates hybridization kinetics, substantially reducing the need for thermal denaturation. This enabled direct RNA capture from crude plasma or whole blood with near-quantitative recovery, outperforming a widely used silica-based kit at low input. Without centrifugation or plasma separation, we detected HIV RNA by RT-qPCR at 25 copies/mL directly from whole blood. We further developed a free energy ({Delta}G)-guided algorithm for mutation-robust probe design, achieving >85% mean recovery across HIV-1 subtypes with a single probe. This work opens low-abundance RNA biomarkers in crude biofluids to ultrasensitive detection, addressing a major barrier to early diagnosis.

papers.title: STARgrid: an open-source pipeline from Visium HD sequencing reads to count matrices
papers.abstract: In Visium HD, transcript positions are computed from sequenced barcodes, which are matched to a list of coordinate barcodes that map to a grid of capture locations. Quantifying reads and assigning their positions have relied on Space Ranger, whose end-user licence prohibits modification and whose published source cannot be redistributed. We present STARgrid, the first open-source pipeline that takes Visium HD FASTQ files from Flex or RNA-seq based quantitation to count matrices at 2, 8 and 16 um; it is part of STAR Suite. On three human slides its output agrees closely with Space Ranger's (correlations of gene totals are at least 0.9989), and STARgrid takes 20-35% less wall time under the tested configurations. STARgrid assigns each read barcode to the coordinate barcode with the most similar sequence, as assessed by edit distance. In an examination of Space Ranger's per-read output on one further slide, Space Ranger does the same for most reads, with two differences. First, where two coordinate barcodes overlap, the shorter being the longer without its first base, Space Ranger records the shorter barcode, although the longer one matches with fewer edits; in all, Space Ranger's location is not among the closest for 0.5980% of the reads that our decoder can place. Second, Space Ranger settles each read on its own, recording one location or none, and leaves 0.2916% of these reads without a location; STARgrid keeps every matching location and chooses among them for each molecule, using all its reads. Our molecule totals are 1.9-7.6% above Space Ranger's. The larger source of this difference is probably that we resolve location for each molecule and not for each read; STAR Suite's own gene assignment and molecule counting may also contribute. The counts that STARgrid adds behave like signal. On H&E images of the same sections they fall in cells at nearly the rate of the counts that both pipelines report. Against an adjacent Xenium section of one slide, our counts are closer to Xenium than Space Ranger's for 15 of the 20 genes of a cancer gene panel that Xenium measures most abundantly (P = 0.0414). The added counts therefore appear to improve the measurement of cancer-associated expression. These results are preliminary, but the method is now open, and every comparison reported here can be repeated, extended and improved upon.

papers.title: Beyond Ramachandran distributions: quantifying secondary structure effects on amino acids and their pairs in the full torsional space
papers.abstract: The Ramachandran diagram has long served for understanding protein secondary structure elements (SSEs), despite the multitude of factors contributing to their occurrence. Starting from recentlyintroduced circula-based multivariate torsion-angle distribution (CBMD) mixture models -- accommodating covariance structure in the full torsion-angle space of amino acids, we define continuous densities for the 20 amino acids and 400 amino-acid pairs in dimension up to 14, conditioned by SSE labels. Projecting these higher-dimensional distributions onto the classical Ramachandran diagram reveals how secondary structures in the protein universe emerge from amino-acid-dependent conformational preferences reflecting influences beyond backbone dihedrals alone. Our analysis links the traditional geometric description of local protein structure to modern statistical models of the full conformational space of amino acids and amino-acidpairs, while providing a framework for generating protein conformations consistent with any given secondary structure environment -- a feature that remains difficult to enforce explicitly in current AI-based generative models.

papers.title: Probabilistic Modelling of Base Editing Efficiency and Bystander Outcome Composition
papers.abstract: Abstract. Base editors install single nucleotide substitutions without a double strand break or donor template, but editing at multiple susceptible positions can generate bystander alleles. Predicting the frequency of an intended outcome therefore requires both editing efficiency and the composition of edited products. Here we present crispAIBE, a probabilistic framework that uses separately trained transformer convolutional networks to predict Dirichlet distributions for editing efficiency and conditional allele composition. Split-conformal density-level regions are calibrated on data reserved from model selection, with composition thresholds fitted by outcome-set size. On held-out data, crispAIBE achieves Pearson correlations of 0.669 for efficiency and 0.896 for composition on measured allele sets, with empirical coverages of 0.902 and 0.906 at a nominal level of 0.90. On the published CRISPRon-BE benchmark, with test protospacers excluded from training, crispAIBE ranks first in seven of eight comparisons under the two-column Pearson statistic and first or second in seven of eight under the rank statistic. Within predicted-efficiency quintiles, the largest- and smallest-region deciles differ 1.9-fold in mean absolute error on average, compared with 1.7-fold for a boundary-distance ranking. When evaluated on U2OS, which was excluded from training, larger predictive regions were associated with larger absolute prediction errors. Local calibration with 100 U2OS protospacers yields median empirical coverage of 0.918 at the nominal 0.90 level. The crispAIBE repository is https://github.com/furkanozdenn/crispAIBE.

papers.title: Multivalent ubiquitin recognition regulates multiple stages of Tau self-assembly
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) has emerged as an important intermediate in the pathological self-assembly of Tau, yet the molecular mechanisms that regulate this process remain incompletely understood. Although ubiquitin is a prominent component of pathological inclusions in tauopathies and other neurodegenerative diseases, its presence has largely been linked to targeting aberrant proteins for proteasomal or autophagic clearance. Here, we identify Tau as a ubiquitin-binding protein and demonstrate that multivalent, non-covalent ubiquitin recognition regulates multiple stages of Tau self-assembly. Biochemical, biophysical, structural, and computational analyses identified four ubiquitin-binding elements within the Tau microtubule-binding repeat region that engage the canonical hydrophobic patch of ubiquitin, providing a structural basis for multivalent recognition of mono- and poly-ubiquitin species. Functionally, mono- and poly-ubiquitin suppress Tau condensate formation while enhancing the liquid-like properties of condensates that persist. In contrast, mono-ubiquitin selectively enhances aggregation of the disease-linked Tau-P301L variant under conditions without detectable LLPS, demonstrating that ubiquitin exerts distinct effects depending on the molecular context and stage of Tau self-assembly. Together, these findings establish non-covalent ubiquitin recognition as a previously unrecognized mechanism regulating Tau phase behavior and aggregation. More broadly, they expand the role of ubiquitin beyond protein quality control, with ubiquitin architecture providing an additional layer of regulation over Tau condensate formation, dynamics, maturation, and aggregation.

papers.title: Scalable Decoupling Contact and Configuration Spaces in a Quantum-Enabled Protein Folding Workflow
papers.abstract: Near-term quantum devices remain constrained by limited qubit counts, noise, and shallow circuit depth, restricting their direct application to peptide folding. This work addresses this limitation through a hybrid quantum-classical framework that separates global contact-space exploration from local configuration-space refinement. The pipeline was evaluated on the p53 transactivation peptide. The peptide was encoded using discrete torsional states and Miyazawa-Jernigan contact potentials. Global conformational search was performed using simulated annealing, followed by fragment-level CVaR-based variational quantum eigensolver refinement. Overlapping fragments were stitched and reconstructed into three-dimensional backbone coordinates for structural comparison. Three independent simulated annealing restarts produced negative-energy conformers. The workflow identified a best global conformer at E = -3.70 MJ using simulated annealing. Fragment-level CVaR-VQE refinement generated 30 candidate conformers across three overlapping fragments, the best assembled conformer reaching E = -2.58 MJ after DP stitching and post-stitch refinement. In this trial, the classical SA solution outperformed the VQE-assembled structure and was selected as the final output. The final 65-atom model was successfully reconstructed, but full-backbone alignment against 1YCR yielded an RMSD of 4.65 angstrom, improving to 2.90 angstrom after trimmed alignment. Our work demonstrates a practical quantum-enabled peptide folding workflow for short, flexible peptides, but the present structural accuracy is insufficient for claims of native fold recovery. Its main value is as an auditable framework for testing NISQ-compatible folding strategies.
