What renders a tumor niche permissive is unknown: chemokines recruit constituent cells but do not specify essential tricellular units. Here we show that the organizing signal is a matrix fragment. Proteoglycan versican (VCAN) proteolysis releases the matrikine versikine, constitutively in germinal center light zones and inducibly in tumor stroma. Versikine activates CD11b+ cDC and expands cDC1 to assemble TLS-archetypal triads, apposed DC:CD4+T:CD8+T units. Versikine-conditioned DC engage progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T cells (Tpex) and Tpex-sustaining, Th1-polarized follicular helper CD4+ T cells. Excess unproteolyzed VCAN inverts this toward DC-Treg crosstalk and Tpex loss. In a prospective PD-1 blockade trial in metastatic colorectal cancer, all VCAN-proteolysis-predominant patients were alive at 4.1-year median follow-up. Versikine (mRNA or recombinant protein) sensitizes proteolysis-weak experimental tumors to PD-L1 blockade. Matrikines organize chemokine-recruited cells into functional intratumoral immune niches.
affiliations: Rush University Medical Center (corresponding author)

papers.title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
papers.abstract: Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

papers.title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
Daily briefing: Rogue ‘jumping genes’ age bigs dogs faster than little ones
Daily briefing: Mathematicians up in arms over OpenAI’s preprint deluge
Chain of Structures: Connecting Reasoning and Generation for Protein Design
papers.abstract: Scientific design requires reasoning in scientific spaces that represent the objects being designed. Building on Scinetics' Chain of Science Tokens, we present chain-of-structures (COS) as a concrete protein-design case study that connects reasoning and generation through explicit structural states. In this technical report, we apply COS to enzyme design, where catalytic function requires precise local geometry within a compatible global fold, making it a demanding test of reasoning from chemical requirements to protein structure. Starting from a reaction specification and target length, COS couples a language reasoning expert with an all-atom generation expert across four rounds: catalytic core, active site, global backbone, and complete sequence and structure. Each reasoning state directly conditions generation, and the resulting structure becomes context for the next decision. Discrete residue constraints and continuous latents connect the two experts, enabling structural supervision of the reasoning interface. On the evaluated benchmark, COS leads the compared baselines on five of six metrics, achieving 57.0% EC3 agreement and a TM-score of 0.729.
affiliations: HKUST (corresponding author)

papers.title: Toxicity by Consortium Revisited: Structural Neighbors and Cross-Family Reach
papers.abstract: A compound's toxicity can be gauged from the toxicities of the compounds it resembles. We showed that in 2003 for rat oral LD50: the compounds in a reference set of 13,645 that most resemble the query form a consortium and vote on its toxicity. This work returns to that method twenty-three years later, on public data, because the reference set used in 2003 is no longer public. Rebuilt on 11,989 curated rat oral LD50 values, the method answers for 67.0% of the held-out compounds carrying an exact value, and 92.1% of those answers land within one log unit; in 2003 the figures were 94% within one log unit on 57.3% of compounds. We then ran it over 28 further endpoints, each recording whether a compound showed a particular toxicity, from cytochrome inhibition to mutagenicity to clinical toxicity: 149,224 measurements on 34,162 compounds. The method answers only when a compound has close enough neighbors, and on those it correctly identifies a median 72.9% of the compounds that showed the toxicity and 96.5% of those that did not. Separately we asked whether a reverse screen carries information about these endpoints beyond molecular size and lipophilicity. We search a compound against a published index of 27,910 ligands solved inside proteins and count the protein families those sites belong to. A compound whose matches reach no protein family inhibits CYP3A4 2.5% of the time; one whose matches span sixteen or more families inhibits 51.0% of the time. Added to heavy atom count, molecular weight and cLogP, the screen raises the mean area under the ROC curve from 0.72 to 0.76 across the 28 endpoints. The OpenADMET consortium has since measured CYP3A4 inhibition on 2,335 compounds, and the same pattern holds. Compounds that resemble known binders of sixteen or more protein families inhibit CYP3A4 24.60% of the time; compounds that resemble no known binder at all inhibit it 5.00% of the time. The more protein families a compound resembles binders of, the more likely it is to inhibit CYP3A4. This association is strong enough to act on before anything is made. Scoring a library on how far its compounds reach across protein families, together with their size and lipophilicity, and setting aside the riskiest fifth removes two thirds of the androgen receptor binders and about half of the CYP3A4 inhibitors. Scoring needs only a two-dimensional structure, with no docking and no conformer generation at query time. Interactive scoring, the data and the pool are at toxpred.ai. Keywords: toxicity prediction; structural similarity; nearest neighbors; reverse screening; target breadth; promiscuity; LD50; cytochrome P450; virtual library triage
affiliations: Eidogen-Sertanty, Inc. (corresponding author)

papers.title: Quantification of grapevine yield losses as a function of downy mildew severity on foliage and cluster
papers.abstract: To quantify the relationship between grapevine disease severity and crop losses at the plant scale, we conducted a three-year field experiment at two sites near Bordeaux (France), monitoring mildews and rots on both foliage and clusters. Preliminary analyses revealed that only downy mildew (DM) significantly impacted yield under our experimental conditions. We capitalized on this single-disease dominance to isolate the effect of DM severity (assessed via standardized AUDPC), on both foliage and clusters, on yield loss at the individual vine scale. At a cluster AUDPC of 5%, yield consistently declined by 24% across all years and sites. Conversely, yield loss at a 5% foliar AUDPC ranged from 9% to 60% depending on the site and year, reflecting a tenfold variation in the damage coefficient. This variability strongly correlated with a moisture risk index computed between the phenological stages of visible inflorescences and pre-ripening berries. Specifically, at 5% foliar AUDPC, the expected yield loss escalated from 9% in a dry season (10th percentile of the index) to 15% in an intermediate season (median), reaching 39% in a wet season (90th percentile). Future research should aim to validate these statistical models across broader climatic, geographic, and agronomic contexts, including the characterization of cultivar-specific responses.
affiliations: INRAE (corresponding author)

papers.title: Reversion to the Meta Body Form of Life after Complete Cell Death in Pure Liquid Water
papers.abstract: The prevailing view holds that simpler animate beings predating the dawn of cellular life once existed, yet they have long since vanished from the present-day Earth. Our hypothesis posits that these animate beings persist to this day. To this end, we devised a long-term experiment spanning over a decade, keeping Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) within a sealed aqueous system of pure water. The findings illustrated that, upon the complete cell death (CCD) of the S. aureus, as cellular remnants progressively succumbed to dissolution, the aqueous solution underwent self-purification, bringing forth a class of lipid bilayer membrane microspheres containing RNA and proteins. These structures maintained long-term sustainable stability within the thermodynamic storm of water molecules and underwent dynamic size fluctuations over time - collectively exhibited phenomena indicative of being "alive". This study reveals that the cell, upon complete cell death, undergoes reversion to a living entity simpler than the cell itself - the Meta Body (MB). The discovery of MB opens an entire re-conceptualization of what death ultimately brings.
affiliations: Congqing Medical University (corresponding author)
